passages: Apple today officially unveiled its new HomeView smart display.
HomeView features a 7-inch square display and comes in two versions: one with a speaker base and another for wall mounting.
The table-top version of HomeView is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.
You can pre-order both today for $299 , with availability beginning November 13.
It will start arriving to customers on November 13.
What do you think of Apple’s new HomeView?
It can also dim to 0.3 nits, making it great for a nightstand.
For audio quality, Apple says HomeView has a “custom-engineered acoustic system” with two full-range drivers in the display, plus a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators.
Apple says the HomeView interface will intelligently adjust based on how far away you are.
It will show “simpler information that’s viewable from across the room” as well as “richer detail” as you step closer.
HomeView can also recognize up to six different people and deliver a “personalized experience” for each one.

This includes a personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. “Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests,” Apple says.
HomeView (Wall Mounted) will be available with a choice of three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home.

Power Mount USB‑C Wall Connector, available starting at $59.95 (U.S.), and Power Mount AC Wired, available starting at $79.95 (U.S.), can be ordered starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app.
There is a collection of “playful and informative” faces for HomeView:
The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background.
Apple says that users with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad can tap into personal context.
Check out 9to5Mac on YouTube for more Apple news:
Here’s everything you need to know about HomeView.
Here are the details on those wall-mounting options from Apple:
By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill.
And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments.

The table-top version of HomeView is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.
You can pre-order both today for $299 , with availability beginning November 13.
It will start arriving to customers on November 13.
What do you think of Apple’s new HomeView?
It can also dim to 0.3 nits, making it great for a nightstand.
For audio quality, Apple says HomeView has a “custom-engineered acoustic system” with two full-range drivers in the display, plus a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators.
Apple says the HomeView interface will intelligently adjust based on how far away you are.
It will show “simpler information that’s viewable from across the room” as well as “richer detail” as you step closer.
HomeView can also recognize up to six different people and deliver a “personalized experience” for each one.

This includes a personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. “Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests,” Apple says.
HomeView (Wall Mounted) will be available with a choice of three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home.

Power Mount USB‑C Wall Connector, available starting at $59.95 (U.S.), and Power Mount AC Wired, available starting at $79.95 (U.S.), can be ordered starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app.
There is a collection of “playful and informative” faces for HomeView:
The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background.
Apple says that users with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad can tap into personal context.
Check out 9to5Mac on YouTube for more Apple news:
Here’s everything you need to know about HomeView.
Here are the details on those wall-mounting options from Apple:
By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill.
And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments.

passages: The HomeView is a 7-inch smart display and speaker that aims to be a central access point for up to six members of a family to access and control Apple’s ecosystem of devices, apps, and the Siri generative AI chatbot that’s currently in beta.
You can also set the screen to automatically adjust its brightness level based on how bright the room is.
Apple started taking preorders for HomeView today.

“With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door.
With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it,” Apple’s announcement said.

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made.
Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”
Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets.
Apple said that Siri requests can run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, where “data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.”

coreStoryFacts.text: It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen.
HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more.
The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad.
A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric.
The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device.
Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface.
To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information.
If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen.
There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning.
Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari.
So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView.
And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that.
HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access.

extraction.body: Two versions will be available in November for $299. It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen. HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more. The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad. The centerpiece of the HomeView is a 7-inch square Liquid Retina display. To me, it looks like an enlarged Apple Watch, and the tabletop version with a base comes in Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink and Space Gray colors. This model has a base that contains a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators to bolster the audio performance of the two full-range drivers in the display. Connecting the screen and base together is a stainless steel hinge that allows you to adjust the viewing angle. If you prefer a wall-mounted option, Apple offers the HomeView without a base, but the overall functionality is the same. Interestingly, there are no buttons on the HomeView; the touchscreen display and your voice are the two ways to interact with the device. The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device. That second number is particularly important in the home, for early mornings or if you plan to place the HomeView on your nightstand. The smart display's main, passive screens are called Faces, which are customizable with things like art, photos and various clock designs. sources.title: Apple’s first smart display is the 7-inch HomeView for $299
passages: The HomeView is a 7-inch smart display and speaker that aims to be a central access point for up to six members of a family to access and control Apple’s ecosystem of devices, apps, and the Siri generative AI chatbot that’s currently in beta.
You can also set the screen to automatically adjust its brightness level based on how bright the room is.
Apple started taking preorders for HomeView today.

“With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door.
With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it,” Apple’s announcement said.

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made.
Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”
Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets.
Apple said that Siri requests can run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, where “data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.”

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made.
Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”
Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets.
Apple said that Siri requests can run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, where “data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.”

extraction.body: Kelly Clarkson reignited a public dispute with Brooklyn novelty store Art of Play after the business challenged her account of an uncomfortable shopping experience. The disagreement has escalated beyond the singer and television personality's original post, with both sides publicly disputing what was said during the encounter. The clash has drawn attention to Art of Play and exposed the impact celebrity criticism can have on small businesses . Newsweek reached out to Clarkson and Art of Play via email for comment on Monday outside regular office hours. Kelly Clarkson performs during the 2023 Rockefeller Center Christmas tree Lighting Ceremony at Rockefeller Center in New York City on November 29, 2023. The dispute began after Clarkson compared her experience at Art of Play to the famous "Big mistake. Huge" shopping scene from Pretty Woman , where Julia Roberts' character is dismissed by store staff based on assumptions about her spending power. Since then, millions of people have viewed the singer's criticism, prompting the Brooklyn business to issue multiple public responses defending its version of events. On Saturday, Clarkson posted on X that she had traveled to Brooklyn specifically to visit the store after spotting some "really rad" items she wanted to buy. According to the singer, a staff member suggested finding her something "comparable" rather than showing her the products she was interested in. Clarkson said she felt she was treated as if she could not afford the merchandise and compared the experience to Pretty Woman . "You just lost a huge sale," she wrote, while encouraging followers to visit the store if they enjoyed being treated like Roberts' character in the movie. The store said the discussion centered on "Molly," a singing and dancing bird automaton that serves as a fixture in its magic shows. Staff said the bird is permanently attached to the wall and is not available for purchase. While expressing sympathy for anyone who has ever felt judged while shopping, Art of Play said it welcomes visitors regardless of whether they spend money and invites customers to interact with its games, toys and puzzles. The business also said it was shocked to become the target of criticism from millions of people who had never visited the shop after being mentioned by a celebrity. The 2002 American Idol winner said a price tag displaying $15,000 was visible near the bird and alleged a staff member told her that the item could be purchased for that amount. Clarkson claimed she was then offered the option of finding something comparable and said the exchange left her feeling patronized. "You're not only rude, you're also a liar," she wrote. Clarkson added that she regularly supports small businesses and argued that their size should not exempt them from criticism if customers are treated poorly. On Monday, Art of Play issued another statement on Instagram , adding fresh details to its account. The store said Clarkson spent about five minutes inside and asked about Molly. According to Art of Play, staff explained that an almost identical bird is owned by Seattle-based artist Bliss Kolb, who would be willing to sell the twin automaton for $15,000. The business said this was the figure discussed during the visit, not the bird mounted on its wall. Art of Play also said it offered to show Clarkson a different singing bird automaton made by a traditional German clockmaker that retails for about $2,000 but claimed she left before seeing it. The shop said it has contacted Clarkson directly in an effort to resolve the disagreement and expressed hope that both sides could eventually laugh about the misunderstanding. As the controversy continued, Art of Play appeared to shift attention toward its reputation among regular customers. "Art of Play is the best place with the best people. While some are staunchly pro-Clarkson in the debate that has since taken over the internet, others have questioned the singer’s motives for calling out the small business across her social media accounts.

From footage from an alternative camera angle, we can see Clarkson then find herself standing in front of the automaton bird, where she then gets the attention of a store employee, who can be seen speaking with the musician and pointing at something by the bird, though it is not clear from the video what he was pointing at. extraction.body: An OpenAI employee was arrested after a " sophisticated recording device " was discovered inside its executive conference room, according to the Department of Justice and a post by the company. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, who is a national of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, was arrested on Oct. 9 in connection with the matter, the DOJ said in a release on Tuesday. The company said an employee planted the device a few days before it was found, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation "moved quickly to make an arrest," the post said. The employee was terminated. FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology." Alfozan is also listed as a partner at Raed Ventures , a venture capital firm that focuses on the Middle East and North Africa, according to its website. The firm announced on Feb. 6, 2025, that H.H. Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, a member of the Saudi royal family, had joined the firm as a venture partner. Alfozan was announced as a venture partner two days later. The Raed announcement for Alfozan lists Meta , Microsoft and SAP as previous roles and said he studied computer science and engineering at MIT. Raed, which is headquartered in the Saudi capital of Riyadh, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," OpenAI said in the post. "We take protecting our technology, data and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance." Alfozan was not authorized to access the executive conference room where the device was found, according to the DOJ. The department said footage showed him near the conference room on multiple days before the device was discovered. The DOJ said that on Oct. 5, he went into the room. The DOJ said a bag was also found in the OpenAI building on or about Oct. 5 that belonged to Alfozan. Inside the bag, security found his wallet, ID and another recording device similar to the one that was in the executive conference room. The department said a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse that "shared multiple identifiers and attributes with Alfozan's own chatbot account" was used to get information about continuous audio recording and Wi-Fi. The DOJ said promps were submitted related to "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device." The device was concealed in toilet paper, and its contents were encrypted, according to the DOJ. This security incident comes as the ChatGPT-maker, along with competitors like Anthropic and other big tech names, faces heightened scrutiny over safety protocols after a series of cyber incidents where autonomous agents escaped testing environments and hacked into outside systems. Last week, OpenAI defended its decision to fire three safety researchers, alleging a "significant breach of trust," saying that the researchers "violated clear policies on handling sensitive information." Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni raised safety concerns in a letter to OpenAI's leadership, saying that communications around their exits "have made our former colleagues afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI." —CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this article. extraction.body: OpenAI said it has alerted the FBI after discovering that an employee allegedly planted a hidden recording device in one of the AI maker’s office executive conference rooms. The employee, named by federal prosecutors as Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was fired and arrested on October 9, about a week after OpenAI discovered the surveillance device. The company said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to understand the “sophisticated” device. OpenAI told TechCrunch that the device contained “advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring,” though it is unclear to what degree this device is technically distinct from other recording devices. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” said OpenAI in its post on X. OpenAI’s spokesperson, Nate Evans, confirmed that the employee started with the AI model maker in July 2025 and worked on the product team. Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said Alfozan was charged with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications — effectively accusing him of covertly recording people’s voice audio without their permission. Prosecutors said OpenAI caught the device after it was inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in OpenAI’s San Francisco office. Per the prosecutors, Alfozan was caught looking behind the television where the recording device was placed, and where OpenAI had placed a camera that allegedly caught the employee. It’s not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to “capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology.” Neither Alfozan nor his attorney could be immediately reached for comment. He faces five years in prison if convicted. When reached, a spokesperson for the FBI reiterated a statement made by Patel. “Protecting American SI innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation’s economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities,” Patel said.

A specialized OpenAI security team—the technical surveillance countermeasures team—first found a recording device on Sept. 30 during a sweep of the conference room, OpenAI told Fortune . OpenAI contacted the FBI after discovering the listening device, which the company says was sophisticated and designed to evade detection. In that conference room, executives frequently held “discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information,” the FBI said. He was an engineering lead, according to his LinkedIn, who worked on OpenAI’s “Agents Platform,” according to his X bio. He formerly worked at Meta for five years, and is a graduate of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (2016) and UC Berkeley (2025). The FBI did not immediately arrest Alfozan upon learning of the device, nor did OpenAI immediately fire him, both of which eventually happened on Oct. 9. He is currently in federal custody and appeared in federal court today, and will appear again on Oct. 19 for a detention hearing. He faces a maximum sentence of 5 years in prison, plus three years supervised release, if convicted. OpenAI said it restricted Alfozan’s access to systems and parts of the office, suspended his network access, placed him on leave, and took his company-issued equipment. OpenAI is using the event to showcase how its technology can help combat these types of threats. The company said it used its models “to understand the device” and figure out which employee had planted it.

Prosecutors said Alfozan had also searched for information about OpenAI's buildings, meeting rooms, calendars, executive locations and external partner meetings. extraction.body: An OpenAI employee was arrested after a " sophisticated recording device " was discovered inside its executive conference room, according to the Department of Justice and a post by the company. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, who is a national of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, was arrested on Oct. 9 in connection with the matter, the DOJ said in a release on Tuesday. The company said an employee planted the device a few days before it was found, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation "moved quickly to make an arrest," the post said. The employee was terminated. FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology." Alfozan is also listed as a partner at Raed Ventures , a venture capital firm that focuses on the Middle East and North Africa, according to its website. The firm announced on Feb. 6, 2025, that H.H. Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, a member of the Saudi royal family, had joined the firm as a venture partner. Alfozan was announced as a venture partner two days later. The Raed announcement for Alfozan lists Meta , Microsoft and SAP as previous roles and said he studied computer science and engineering at MIT. Raed, which is headquartered in the Saudi capital of Riyadh, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," OpenAI said in the post. "We take protecting our technology, data and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance." Alfozan was not authorized to access the executive conference room where the device was found, according to the DOJ. The department said footage showed him near the conference room on multiple days before the device was discovered. The DOJ said that on Oct. 5, he went into the room. The DOJ said a bag was also found in the OpenAI building on or about Oct. 5 that belonged to Alfozan. Inside the bag, security found his wallet, ID and another recording device similar to the one that was in the executive conference room. The department said a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse that "shared multiple identifiers and attributes with Alfozan's own chatbot account" was used to get information about continuous audio recording and Wi-Fi. The DOJ said promps were submitted related to "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device." The device was concealed in toilet paper, and its contents were encrypted, according to the DOJ. This security incident comes as the ChatGPT-maker, along with competitors like Anthropic and other big tech names, faces heightened scrutiny over safety protocols after a series of cyber incidents where autonomous agents escaped testing environments and hacked into outside systems. Last week, OpenAI defended its decision to fire three safety researchers, alleging a "significant breach of trust," saying that the researchers "violated clear policies on handling sensitive information." Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni raised safety concerns in a letter to OpenAI's leadership, saying that communications around their exits "have made our former colleagues afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI." —CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this article. A recording device was discovered in a key conference room at OpenAI, the California-based developer of ChatGPT. Following an arrest, the FBI is continuing its investigation.

An employee of OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT, is suspected of planting a listening device in one of the company’s conference rooms. Following his arrest, the FBI is investigating. The 35-year-old Saudi citizen was arrested, according to statements from the AI company and the U.S. Department of Justice. Trade secrets were often discussed in the company’s conference room.

According to investigators, the recording device discovered two weeks ago had been placed in the conference room in San Francisco about two days earlier. It was reportedly plugged into a TV's USB port, wrapped in toilet paper.

According to the ministry, the arrested employee was caught on security cameras in late September near the conference room, to which he was not authorized to have access. Investigators also released a photo showing him later trying to look behind the television.

According to the ministry, inquiries about recording devices were made through a chatbot account belonging to the wife of the OpenAI employee. The chat history reportedly also contained details matching the characteristics of the listening device discovered in the conference room. If convicted, the employee faced up to five years in prison and a fine equivalent to just over 230,000 Swiss francs.

U.S. Intelligence Coordinator Jay Clayton emphasized in the statement that the case demonstrates how important it is for U.S. national security to win the race to develop artificial intelligence. President Donald Trump had also entrusted Clayton with a key role in AI oversight. Just recently, an AI researcher—who has now come forward as a whistleblower—expressed the suspicion that Chinese spies had infiltrated the major AI labs at OpenAI and Anthropic. He did not present any evidence to support this claim.

The employee was identified as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national. Alfozan is charged with using or endeavoring to use a device to intercept oral communications, according to a press release from the Department of Justice. Alfozan didn’t have access to this room, but CCTV footage allegedly showed him “near the executive conference room on multiple dates prior to the device’s discovery,” according to the DOJ. Additionally, the DOJ claims OpenAI security discovered a bag Alfozan left in another room inside the company’s office, where they found his wallet, ID, and another recording device. We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work. > At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated. > We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance. It added that meetings within the conference room “frequently involved discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial and strategic information, including proprietary research, product plans and business-development opportunities.”
Following Alfozan’s arrest, company officials discovered a bag belonging to him that contained a second recording device identical to the one found earlier.

Or, can you not find an app that fits a weirdly specific need?
Now you can make custom apps for your own Android phone, even if you have zero coding experience.
One Tuesday, Google announced that anyone with a standard Google account can build personal apps in Google AI Studio.
These apps will run on your own device, launched from a private part of Google Play, and won’t be included in the public Play Store.
You’ll be able to share your apps with close family and friends in the coming months, but you don’t have to.
Custom Android apps make app development a much more personal and potentially user-friendly experience.

extraction.body: Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private. These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator. The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android. Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use. These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android. Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up. “That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.” In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store. And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews. Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates. Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations. The changes are rolling out alongside Google Play’s new support for an age-range feature that allows parents to share their child’s age range, but not their exact birthdate, with developers to get an age-appropriate experience. sources.title: Google Play Vibe Coding Lets Users Build Private Android Apps - Innovation Village
passages: Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store.
The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution.
Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies.
Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices.
Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account.
Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly.
For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods.
It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases.
Google is also updating how users discover applications and games.
Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps.
The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves.
Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment.
This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code.
The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on.
If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves.
As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful.

extraction.body: Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store. The new feature from Google makes it easier for people to turn everyday needs into custom applications, even without traditional programming skills. Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices. Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account. Initially, the feature is rolling out to adults aged 18 and older in the United States and select markets. These apps will remain private, absent from public Play Store search results and accessible only to their creators. Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly. The update reflects a broader change in software development. As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful. They can be built for one person, one household or a specific problem that existing software does not adequately address. Until now, people experimenting with AI-generated Android applications faced a gap between creating an app and conveniently using it on their own devices. They could build web applications or work through more technical installation processes, but distributing a native Android app through Google Play traditionally required a developer account and additional publishing steps. Google’s new feature simplifies that process. Users can describe an idea to Gemini through Google AI Studio, refine the generated application and launch it for personal use. The potential applications are straightforward. Someone could create a specialised expense tracker that matches their budgeting habits, a personalised workout log or a household organiser tailored to their family. A student could build a revision tool around a particular subject, while a small business owner could experiment with a simple inventory application. These tools do not need to compete with established apps or attract thousands of downloads. Their value comes from solving a specific problem for the person who created them. This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code. It does not eliminate the need to test software or understand its limitations, but it lowers the technical barrier to experimentation. The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution. Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies. Users who want to distribute their creations publicly must move to a professional developer account and pass the platform’s standard trust and safety reviews. This creates a clearer path from experimentation to publication. A personal project can begin as a private tool, be shared with a small group and eventually become a public product if it proves useful. For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods. It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases. The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves. Google is effectively moving beyond the idea that every useful application must first become a conventional public product. However, the distinction between personal and public apps remains important. An app generated for individual use may contain bugs, mishandle information or produce unreliable results. Private distribution does not automatically make software secure or accurate. Users will still need to be cautious about the permissions they grant and the information they enter. Google is also updating how users discover applications and games. Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps. Google is also bringing Play Store app links into Gemini conversations, allowing the assistant to surface relevant applications directly. Together, these changes show how Google is adapting the Play Store for an environment increasingly shaped by AI. The technology is influencing not only how software is built, but also how people find, personalise and use it. The larger opportunity is a shift away from one-size-fits-all software. Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment. AI-generated personal apps could address smaller, more specific needs that commercial developers have little incentive to pursue. Yet creating software cheaply does not guarantee that it will work well. As more people generate applications, testing, maintenance, privacy and security will become increasingly important. Users may be able to create their own solutions, but they will still need ways to recognise when those solutions are unreliable. Google’s new feature is an early step towards that more personal software environment. It does not replace professional development or remove the need for platform oversight. Instead, it makes the space between having an idea and using a working Android app considerably smaller. The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on. If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves. A writer exploring the intersections of innovation, culture and fashion across Africa

sources.title: Google Play now lets you ‘vibe code’ and launch your own personal Android apps
passages: "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play.

Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account.
Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update.

According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required.

Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC.
Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog.
Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse.

However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release.
Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment.

extraction.body: Google is rolling out a massive wave of updates to the Google Play Store today, and the headline feature completely changes how everyday users can build and run software on their devices. According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required. Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update. "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play. Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account. No Developer Account Needed: You don't have to pay registration fees or jump through publishing hoops to get your custom app onto your phone. Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog. Future Sharing: Rolling out today in the U.S. (for users 18+), the feature is currently limited to your own device. However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release. Smarter discovery and Googlebook optimizations Alongside personal app creation, Google is overhauling how you find content across different form factors and inside the store itself: Built for Googlebook & Beyond: The Play Store is adapting better to non-phone screens. On the new Googlebook platform, apps optimized for large screens are now pushed front and center. Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse. Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment. Additionally, "Play in Gemini" is rolling out soon to bring app and game recommendations directly into your Gemini chats. Sports Topic Pages: You can now follow live scores and jump directly into streaming apps for major soccer leagues, including the Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and MLS. "Gamer DNA," 48-hour Sprints, and PC expansions Mobile and PC gaming on Google Play also received a hefty set of community and discovery upgrades: Game Finder & Gamer DNA: Rolling out in the U.S. today, Game Finder analyzes how you play and your stated preferences (mechanics, art styles, genres) to build your "Gamer DNA." It uses this profile alongside data from similar players to recommend titles that actually match your taste, rather than just pushing what is popular. You can also curate and soon share custom "Game Playlists." Sprints & Sidekick: Available globally today, "Sprints" are fast-paced, 48-hour micro-challenges that match you with groups of two to five players. Community Posts: Game detail pages now feature a built-in Q&A forum with automatic language translation so players can help each other out directly in the store. Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC. Google is also expanding free limited-time Game Trials to PC titles. Finally, Google is adding a new Family Link feature that lets parents share a child's general age range directly with apps to ensure age-appropriate experiences without oversharing personal data. Most of these updates, alongside this week's Play Fest points event, are beginning their rollout today. Be sure to check your Play Store app over the next few days to see the new layout and tools in action.

coreStoryFacts.text: Are you tired of ad overload in free, single-task apps?
Or, can you not find an app that fits a weirdly specific need?
Now you can make custom apps for your own Android phone, even if you have zero coding experience.
One Tuesday, Google announced that anyone with a standard Google account can build personal apps in Google AI Studio.
These apps will run on your own device, launched from a private part of Google Play, and won’t be included in the public Play Store.
You’ll be able to share your apps with close family and friends in the coming months, but you don’t have to.
Custom Android apps make app development a much more personal and potentially user-friendly experience.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android
It just got a whole lot easier to vibe code the exact Android app you need - no developer experience required.
Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday.
A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs.
That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.
But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.”
In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends.
Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications.
Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations.
Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use.
Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store.
The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution.
Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies.
Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices.
Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account.

A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs.
That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.
But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.”
In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends.
Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications.
Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations.

extraction.body: Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private. These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator. The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android. Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use. These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android. Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up. “That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.” In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store. And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews. Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates. Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations. The changes are rolling out alongside Google Play’s new support for an age-range feature that allows parents to share their child’s age range, but not their exact birthdate, with developers to get an age-appropriate experience. sources.title: Google Play Vibe Coding Lets Users Build Private Android Apps - Innovation Village
passages: Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store.
The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution.
Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies.
Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices.
Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account.
Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly.
For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods.
It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases.
Google is also updating how users discover applications and games.
Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps.
The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves.
Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment.
This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code.
The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on.
If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves.
As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful.

extraction.body: Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store. The new feature from Google makes it easier for people to turn everyday needs into custom applications, even without traditional programming skills. Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices. Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account. Initially, the feature is rolling out to adults aged 18 and older in the United States and select markets. These apps will remain private, absent from public Play Store search results and accessible only to their creators. Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly. The update reflects a broader change in software development. As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful. They can be built for one person, one household or a specific problem that existing software does not adequately address. Until now, people experimenting with AI-generated Android applications faced a gap between creating an app and conveniently using it on their own devices. They could build web applications or work through more technical installation processes, but distributing a native Android app through Google Play traditionally required a developer account and additional publishing steps. Google’s new feature simplifies that process. Users can describe an idea to Gemini through Google AI Studio, refine the generated application and launch it for personal use. The potential applications are straightforward. Someone could create a specialised expense tracker that matches their budgeting habits, a personalised workout log or a household organiser tailored to their family. A student could build a revision tool around a particular subject, while a small business owner could experiment with a simple inventory application. These tools do not need to compete with established apps or attract thousands of downloads. Their value comes from solving a specific problem for the person who created them. This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code. It does not eliminate the need to test software or understand its limitations, but it lowers the technical barrier to experimentation. The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution. Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies. Users who want to distribute their creations publicly must move to a professional developer account and pass the platform’s standard trust and safety reviews. This creates a clearer path from experimentation to publication. A personal project can begin as a private tool, be shared with a small group and eventually become a public product if it proves useful. For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods. It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases. The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves. Google is effectively moving beyond the idea that every useful application must first become a conventional public product. However, the distinction between personal and public apps remains important. An app generated for individual use may contain bugs, mishandle information or produce unreliable results. Private distribution does not automatically make software secure or accurate. Users will still need to be cautious about the permissions they grant and the information they enter. Google is also updating how users discover applications and games. Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps. Google is also bringing Play Store app links into Gemini conversations, allowing the assistant to surface relevant applications directly. Together, these changes show how Google is adapting the Play Store for an environment increasingly shaped by AI. The technology is influencing not only how software is built, but also how people find, personalise and use it. The larger opportunity is a shift away from one-size-fits-all software. Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment. AI-generated personal apps could address smaller, more specific needs that commercial developers have little incentive to pursue. Yet creating software cheaply does not guarantee that it will work well. As more people generate applications, testing, maintenance, privacy and security will become increasingly important. Users may be able to create their own solutions, but they will still need ways to recognise when those solutions are unreliable. Google’s new feature is an early step towards that more personal software environment. It does not replace professional development or remove the need for platform oversight. Instead, it makes the space between having an idea and using a working Android app considerably smaller. The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on. If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves. A writer exploring the intersections of innovation, culture and fashion across Africa

Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account.

No Developer Account Needed: You don't have to pay registration fees or jump through publishing hoops to get your custom app onto your phone. Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog. Future Sharing: Rolling out today in the U.S. (for users 18+), the feature is currently limited to your own device. However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release. Smarter discovery and Googlebook optimizations Alongside personal app creation, Google is overhauling how you find content across different form factors and inside the store itself: Built for Googlebook & Beyond: The Play Store is adapting better to non-phone screens. On the new Googlebook platform, apps optimized for large screens are now pushed front and center. Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse. "Gamer DNA," 48-hour Sprints, and PC expansions Mobile and PC gaming on Google Play also received a hefty set of community and discovery upgrades: Game Finder & Gamer DNA: Rolling out in the U.S. today, Game Finder analyzes how you play and your stated preferences (mechanics, art styles, genres) to build your "Gamer DNA." It uses this profile alongside data from similar players to recommend titles that actually match your taste, rather than just pushing what is popular. You can also curate and soon share custom "Game Playlists." Sprints & Sidekick: Available globally today, "Sprints" are fast-paced, 48-hour micro-challenges that match you with groups of two to five players. Finally, Google is adding a new Family Link feature that lets parents share a child's general age range directly with apps to ensure age-appropriate experiences without oversharing personal data. Most of these updates, alongside this week's Play Fest points event, are beginning their rollout today. Be sure to check your Play Store app over the next few days to see the new layout and tools in action.

FFR and FFAI will host a joint new product launch event on October 14, featuring FF Nova, FF Nova Mini, the EAI Education Ecosystem Brain and Curriculum Skills 2.0, and the FF Nova Developer Reinforcement Learning Platform.
FFAI and AIAA will co-host an AIAA LA Seminar at FFAI headquarters to address Frontier Technology in Engineering and Academia.
More than 50 scholars and professors from leading universities and the AI field were invited to the event.

(NASDAQ: FFR ) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI (EAI) robotics company that is in the process of acquiring the FF EAI Robotics business. Upon completion of the acquisition, the Company will focus on the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization, and deployment of intelligent robotic technologies, products, and industry solutions. The Company is committed to building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of EAI Brain & Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions, and EAI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," the Company aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified EAI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The FF EAI Robotics business has already achieved commercial deliveries of humanoid and biomimetic robotic products. Through its multi-form-factor robotic products, EAI technology platform, closed-loop data capabilities, and industry solutions, the business continues to advance the scaled adoption of robotics across real-world applications. The Company also operates RoboShare, a robot-sharing and services platform designed to connect robotic assets, service capabilities, customer demand, and ecosystem partners, further strengthening its robotics commercialization and service ecosystem. Faraday Future Announces FF EAI Robotics’ Employee Incentive Plan to Allocate Approximately 25% of Its Outstanding Shares for Stock Options for Its Core Team, Aiming to Establish an Industry-First Partnership Model Los Angeles, CA (September 23, 2026) – Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. (“FFR”). FF EAI Robotics is allocating approximately 25% of the capitalization of FF EAI Robotics on a fully diluted basis as the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan to provide long-term equity incentives for the Company’s core management team, key leaders, and key employees. The proposed plan is intended to further strengthen FF’s robotics strategy and help FF EAI Robotics establish a partnership model in the robotics industry. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI. “The equity incentive plan is intended to create a long-term incentive and value-sharing mechanism,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. “By linking the core team’s long-term interests to the growth of our robotics business and enterprise value, we aim to align the interests of our team, the Company and our stockholders. We believe this will encourage a partnership mindset, sustained commitment and long-term value creation.” FF aims to build the world’s only “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World. Its “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem is taking shape, and Robot World 2.0 is complete. Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms. At its 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch, FF launched nine EAI Device configurations across two robot forms, three series and five models: FF All-New Futurist, FF Master Mini, FX Aegis Hyper, FX Aegis Mega and FX Aegis Classic Ultra-W. All nine are now available for sale and delivery. FF also launched four Industry Productivity Solutions for K-12 Education, Research, Security and Inspection. Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy. First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront. Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry. Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector. FF focuses on two major product strategies within the Embodied AI (EAI) robotics business: EAI humanoid and bionic robots, and EAI automotive-focused robots. By building a “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem comprising the EAI Brain and Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions and the EAI Data Factory, FF aims to create an evolutionary flywheel: scaled device delivery, data collection and training, continuous evolution of the EAI Brain, stronger product capabilities, and even larger-scale delivery and deployment. Through this flywheel, FF seeks to maximize its commercial value and advance the development of Physical AI. Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders

FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy.

First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront.

Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry.

Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector.

Founded in 2014, Faraday Future (FF) is a U.S.-based Physical AI ecosystem company dedicated to reshaping the future of robotics and mobility solutions through AI innovation and technologies. FF focuses on two major product strategies within the Embodied AI (EAI) robotics business: EAI humanoid and bionic robots, and EAI automotive-focused robots. By building a “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem comprising the EAI Brain and Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions and the EAI Data Factory, FF aims to create an evolutionary flywheel: scaled device delivery, data collection and training, continuous evolution of the EAI Brain, stronger product capabilities, and even larger-scale delivery and deployment. Through this flywheel, FF seeks to maximize its commercial value and advance the development of Physical AI.

(“FF Robotics”). Each Award of stock options to the foregoing officers vests over four years, with 25% of the Award vesting on the 6-month anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date of September 22,2026, and the remaining 75% of the Award vesting 36 monthly installments, the first of which vests on the first anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date and each of the remaining 35 vesting on the same day of each succeeding calendar month.
