The New Products Advance LG's Zero Labor Home Vision Across Indoor and Outdoor Living Spaces LG Electronics and Apple announced the seven smart home accessories for the Apple Home Collection, including indoor and outdoor cameras, a video doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat and temperature sensor. The new products are co-developed by LG Electronics and Apple, and work seamlessly with Apple devices. The collaboration goes beyond device compatibility, combining LG's deep knowledge of product and homes with Apple's platform expertise to deliver a more intuitive and integrated smart home experience. These products work together seamlessly to help users with their daily routines, including monitoring and protecting their homes while away. NEW YORK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics (LG) today announced a range of smart home accessories co-developed with Apple for the Apple Home Collection, including indoor and outdoor cameras, and a video doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat and temperature sensor. The new products are designed to make the everyday home experience simpler, more reliable and seamlessly connected and private in Apple Home. These smart home accessories represent LG's commitment to creating connected and adaptive experiences. They also advance the company's ambition to simplify everyday living by reducing the need for manual intervention and enabling more intuitive interactions between customers and their environments. "Creating a truly connected home requires products that work seamlessly together," said Kihyun Jung, head of the Platform Business Center at the LG Home Appliance Solution Company. "By bringing LG's expertise in home appliances and the home environment together with the Apple Home, we are creating intuitive, integrated experiences that fit naturally into customers' daily lives." "Apple has always focused on making products and experiences that are seamless and intuitive, and protect our users' privacy — and that matters more than ever in the home," said Matthew Costello, Apple's vice president of Hardware Engineering. "Combining our hardware and software expertise with LG's deep understanding of the home and connected living lets us build smart home experiences that are simpler to set up, are easier to control, and work effortlessly." Moving Beyond Connectivity to Co-Develop Products and User Experiences Moving beyond just device compatibility, Apple and LG developed these new products together from the early product planning stage, collaborating on hardware, software and user experiences. Each product is designed with a consistent user experience in mind to streamline setup and control. Rather than simply linking individual products through a platform, the accessories are designed to work together. Using the Home app or Siri to control a single "Good Morning" scene can simultaneously adjust the thermostat and tilt an indoor camera down while a user is getting ready.1 And each accessory is encrypted end-to-end in Apple Home, so only users and the people they choose can access their home data. Introducing New Indoor and Outdoor Cameras, a Video Doorbell, Smart Lock, Thermostat and Temperature Sensor Starting in December, with select accessories coming early next year, LG and Apple are launching the full lineup in the United States and Canada, including indoor and outdoor cameras, a video doorbell, a smart lock, a thermostat and a temperature sensor with support for Apple Home and LG ThinQ apps.1 In the United Kingdom, indoor and outdoor cameras and a video doorbell will be available starting December.2 Cameras LG's new indoor and outdoor cameras deliver clear imaging, intelligent detection and privacy-focused controls to help users monitor what matters around their homes. With up to 2.5K video resolution, low-light color night vision, and wide-angle coverage, the cameras provide clear views during the day and at night. Using intelligence, each camera recognizes people, pets, vehicles and motion, helping deliver more relevant alerts and reducing unnecessary notifications. Users can also block selected areas from view and recording, while built-in local storage provides greater control over how recorded footage is stored and reviewed. LG Indoor Cam Plug-In : A wide 160° field of view captures more of the room in a single frame, while a privacy tilt mechanism and physical controls provide a visible and intuitive way to control monitoring when it is not needed. LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In : The camera provides reliable outdoor monitoring with low light color night vision, and 2.5K resolution, helping users maintain a clear view around the home day and night. LG Floodlight Cam : The camera adds dual adaptive floodlights that automatically illuminate the surrounding area when activity is detected, combining outdoor monitoring and lighting in one integrated home security solution. LG Video Doorbell Wired LG Video Doorbell Wired brings clear visibility, more relevant alerts and everyday convenience to the front door. Its dual-camera system combines a 2.5K front camera and a Full HD bottom camera, capturing separate views of visitors, packages and key areas around the entryway for broader coverage. It can also identify people, vehicles, pets and packages and play a helpful chime through Apple HomeView, HomePod or HomePod mini. Low-light color night vision and two-way talk also help users see and respond to activity at their door. LG Smart Deadbolt Lock LG Smart Deadbolt Lock combines smart access, minimal design and everyday convenience, led by hands-free unlocking with home key on a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch and advanced Ultra-Wideband technology. The lock recognizes an authorized user's location and movement to support reliable hands-free entry. NFC tap, PIN code and a physical key provide additional ways to unlock the door, while built-in door sensing and real-time app notifications help users monitor door status and security events. LG Smart Thermostat and LG Temperature Sensor LG Smart Thermostat combines energy efficiency, intuitive design to make home comfort more adaptive and efficient. Adaptive Temperature from Apple can adjust heating and cooling based on headed home, away from home or sleeping. When paired with optional LG Temperature Sensor devices placed in other rooms, the system can monitor temperature and humidity across multiple spaces to support more consistent comfort throughout the home. Advanced sensing algorithms are designed to reduce measurement errors and detect indoor temperature changes in real time, while Matter over Thread enables low-power, responsive connectivity with fewer connection delays and offline disruptions. In the U.S., Clean Energy Guidance from Apple can help optimize energy use based on grid carbon intensity. Through supported utility-provider integrations, LG Smart Thermostat can also shift operation toward lower-cost periods. Privacy in Apple Home Privacy is foundational to Apple Home. Camera footage and personal data in the Home app is stored end-to-end encrypted and never accessible to LG or Apple. 1 Use of the new IoT products requires an Apple home hub, like HomePod, HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K or Apple HomeView. The new IoT products, the LG ThinQ, and the Apple Home require a Wi-Fi connection. Available services, features and compatibility may vary depending on product model, region and country. 2 Product availability, including availability at retail stores, may vary by region and country. LG Electronics is a global innovator in technology and consumer electronics with a presence in almost every country and an international workforce of more than 75,000. LG's four Companies – Home Appliance Solution, Media Entertainment Solution, Vehicle Solution and the Eco Solution – combined for global revenue of over KRW 89 trillion in 2025. LG is a leading manufacturer of consumer and commercial products ranging from TVs, home appliances, air solutions, monitors, automotive components and solutions, and its premium LG SIGNATURE and intelligent LG ThinQ brands are familiar names the world over. Visit www.lg.com/global/newsroom for the latest news.

NEW YORK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics (LG) today announced a range of smart home accessories co-developed with Apple for the Apple Home Collection, including indoor and outdoor cameras, and a video doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat and temperature sensor. The new products are designed to make the everyday home experience simpler, more reliable and seamlessly connected and private in Apple Home.

These smart home accessories represent LG's commitment to creating connected and adaptive experiences. They also advance the company's ambition to simplify everyday living by reducing the need for manual intervention and enabling more intuitive interactions between customers and their environments.

"Creating a truly connected home requires products that work seamlessly together," said Kihyun Jung, head of the Platform Business Center at the LG Home Appliance Solution Company. "By bringing LG's expertise in home appliances and the home environment together with the Apple Home, we are creating intuitive, integrated experiences that fit naturally into customers' daily lives."

"Apple has always focused on making products and experiences that are seamless and intuitive, and protect our users' privacy — and that matters more than ever in the home," said Matthew Costello, Apple's vice president of Hardware Engineering. "Combining our hardware and software expertise with LG's deep understanding of the home and connected living lets us build smart home experiences that are simpler to set up, are easier to control, and work effortlessly."
Moving Beyond Connectivity to Co-Develop Products and User Experiences
Moving beyond just device compatibility, Apple and LG developed these new products together from the early product planning stage, collaborating on hardware, software and user experiences.

Each product is designed with a consistent user experience in mind to streamline setup and control. Rather than simply linking individual products through a platform, the accessories are designed to work together. Using the Home app or Siri to control a single "Good Morning" scene can simultaneously adjust the thermostat and tilt an indoor camera down while a user is getting ready.1 And each accessory is encrypted end-to-end in Apple Home, so only users and the people they choose can access their home data.
Introducing New Indoor and Outdoor Cameras, a Video Doorbell, Smart Lock, Thermostat and Temperature Sensor

Starting in December, with select accessories coming early next year, LG and Apple are launching the full lineup in the United States and Canada, including indoor and outdoor cameras, a video doorbell, a smart lock, a thermostat and a temperature sensor with support for Apple Home and LG ThinQ apps.1 In the United Kingdom, indoor and outdoor cameras and a video doorbell will be available starting December.2

Cameras LG's new indoor and outdoor cameras deliver clear imaging, intelligent detection and privacy-focused controls to help users monitor what matters around their homes. With up to 2.5K video resolution, low-light color night vision, and wide-angle coverage, the cameras provide clear views during the day and at night. Using intelligence, each camera recognizes people, pets, vehicles and motion, helping deliver more relevant alerts and reducing unnecessary notifications. Users can also block selected areas from view and recording, while built-in local storage provides greater control over how recorded footage is stored and reviewed.

LG Indoor Cam Plug-In : A wide 160° field of view captures more of the room in a single frame, while a privacy tilt mechanism and physical controls provide a visible and intuitive way to control monitoring when it is not needed.
LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In : The camera provides reliable outdoor monitoring with low light color night vision, and 2.5K resolution, helping users maintain a clear view around the home day and night.

LG Floodlight Cam : The camera adds dual adaptive floodlights that automatically illuminate the surrounding area when activity is detected, combining outdoor monitoring and lighting in one integrated home security solution.

LG Video Doorbell Wired LG Video Doorbell Wired brings clear visibility, more relevant alerts and everyday convenience to the front door. Its dual-camera system combines a 2.5K front camera and a Full HD bottom camera, capturing separate views of visitors, packages and key areas around the entryway for broader coverage. It can also identify people, vehicles, pets and packages and play a helpful chime through Apple HomeView, HomePod or HomePod mini. Low-light color night vision and two-way talk also help users see and respond to activity at their door.

LG Smart Deadbolt Lock LG Smart Deadbolt Lock combines smart access, minimal design and everyday convenience, led by hands-free unlocking with home key on a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch and advanced Ultra-Wideband technology. The lock recognizes an authorized user's location and movement to support reliable hands-free entry. NFC tap, PIN code and a physical key provide additional ways to unlock the door, while built-in door sensing and real-time app notifications help users monitor door status and security events.

LG Smart Thermostat and LG Temperature Sensor LG Smart Thermostat combines energy efficiency, intuitive design to make home comfort more adaptive and efficient. Adaptive Temperature from Apple can adjust heating and cooling based on headed home, away from home or sleeping. When paired with optional LG Temperature Sensor devices placed in other rooms, the system can monitor temperature and humidity across multiple spaces to support more consistent comfort throughout the home. Advanced sensing algorithms are designed to reduce measurement errors and detect indoor temperature changes in real time, while Matter over Thread enables low-power, responsive connectivity with fewer connection delays and offline disruptions. In the U.S., Clean Energy Guidance from Apple can help optimize energy use based on grid carbon intensity. Through supported utility-provider integrations, LG Smart Thermostat can also shift operation toward lower-cost periods.
Privacy in Apple Home Privacy is foundational to Apple Home. Camera footage and personal data in the Home app is stored end-to-end encrypted and never accessible to LG or Apple.

1 Use of the new IoT products requires an Apple home hub, like HomePod, HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K or Apple HomeView. The new IoT products, the LG ThinQ, and the Apple Home require a Wi-Fi connection. Available services, features and compatibility may vary depending on product model, region and country.
2 Product availability, including availability at retail stores, may vary by region and country.

LG Electronics is a global innovator in technology and consumer electronics with a presence in almost every country and an international workforce of more than 75,000. LG's four Companies – Home Appliance Solution, Media Entertainment Solution, Vehicle Solution and the Eco Solution – combined for global revenue of over KRW 89 trillion in 2025. LG is a leading manufacturer of consumer and commercial products ranging from TVs, home appliances, air solutions, monitors, automotive components and solutions, and its premium LG SIGNATURE and intelligent LG ThinQ brands are familiar names the world over. CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced Apple Home Collection, a new lineup of smart home accessories — including indoor and outdoor cameras, thermostats, temperature sensors, and a video doorbell and door lock — designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. 1 These new accessories are simple to set up starting with one tap with iPhone, and everything is managed through the Apple Home app — no separate app or account required. Each accessory is encrypted end-to-end in Apple Home, so only users and the people they choose can access their home data.

Building on the thousands of Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories available today, Apple Home Collection offers customers a new array of recommended products to better understand what’s happening inside and outside their home, manage access, and keep the temperature just right throughout the day. Availability for all products begins in December, with select accessories available starting early 2027.

“Apple Home Collection makes it easy to choose smart home accessories with confidence,” said Matthew Costello, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “Working closely with industry leaders LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, we designed every accessory to work seamlessly with Apple Home, so managing your home is simple, reliable, and private.”

Works with Apple Home and Matter certification have allowed a wide array of third-party accessories to connect with Apple’s smart home ecosystem for years, and Apple Home Collection takes it even further. Apple worked closely with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric to create an integrated Apple Home experience across the new product lineup. And like all accessories in Apple Home, Apple Home Collection products are designed for privacy, with Home app data encrypted end-to-end, so LG Electronics, Schneider Electric, and Apple can’t read it.

These new Apple Home Collection products feature a clean, minimal aesthetic and premium materials, with every detail considered, from how they mount and adjust to how they look and feel alongside Apple products throughout the home. Each product can be set up starting with a single tap with iPhone, controlled entirely from the Home app and using Siri, and work as either standalone accessories or together as a connected system.

“LG Electronics has spent decades developing technologies and products designed around the way people live,” said Kihyun Jung, LG Electronics’ executive vice president. “Working closely with Apple, we’ve co-created a more connected, intuitive, and convenient home experience for our customers.”

“As a global leader in energy technology, we are proud to bring our experience in innovative and advanced climate control to Apple Home,” said Olivier Blum, Schneider Electric’s CEO. “Schneider Home’s new Smart Thermostat is a true collaboration with Apple to give customers a seamless way to help manage their home’s energy use, effortlessly blending efficiency with everyday comfort and simplicity.”

LG’s lineup of four cameras gives users a private and intelligent way to monitor their homes when using a home hub like Apple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K. Every camera captures up to 2.5K resolution video and recognizes people, familiar faces, pets, vehicles, and packages, with video history securely stored in users’ supported iCloud+ plan, so there’s no separate camera subscription. 2

Each camera works with iCloud+, giving users access to 10 days’ worth of event video history. On eligible iCloud+ plans, Apple Intelligence adds automatic video descriptions that summarize what’s happening in a clip, along with the ability to search footage using natural, descriptive language. 3 Built-in storage keeps cameras recording even when Wi-Fi goes down, and improvements to the way footage is captured and stored ensure detected moments aren’t missed during a network outage. Users can view live footage and camera activity at any time right from the Home app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV 4K, or HomeView — with quick live snapshots that give an at-a-glance view without needing to open a full livestream.

LG’s Smart Deadbolt Lock brings a new level of convenience to home access. Using Ultra Wideband technology, the lock can tell how close a user is and when they’re approaching the door. As a user with a home key on a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch walks up, the door unlocks automatically, with no tapping required. For flexibility, users can also tap to unlock with an iPhone or Apple Watch, use an integrated PIN pad, or rely on a hidden backup key slot. The lock can sense if the door has been opened, closed, or tampered with, alerting users if it’s open even while locked. Guest access can also be shared directly through the Home app, making it simple to grant a dog walker, house sitter, or visiting family member their own way in.

Controls in the Home app allow the doorbell and lock to work together as a front-door system — letting users see who’s there and unlock the door in a single view or by asking Siri. When a visitor rings the bell, a chime sounds through HomeView, HomePod, or HomePod mini, and a notification appears on the user’s Apple devices, like iPhone or iPad. From wherever they are, users can see who’s at the door, speak to the visitor, and unlock the door for them. The new smart lock is Matter compatible and supports Aliro, working entirely locally so core access functions continue even without an internet connection.

Two new Smart Thermostats are available — one from LG Electronics and one from Schneider Electric — so users can choose the product that best fits their home’s broader energy ecosystem. Using on-device intelligence from iPhone, Adaptive Temperature in the Home app automatically adjusts the thermostats based on whether someone is at home, winding down at night, or away, ensuring the home is always at the right temperature without any manual scheduling.

In the contiguous U.S., Clean Energy Guidance can shift heating and cooling to cleaner, lower-cost periods for users with a compatible utility plan, and the Home app displays usage insights over time, including peak and off-peak rate information. The new thermostats can read temperature and humidity across multiple rooms using LG Electronics’ and Schneider Electric’s new standalone temperature and humidity sensors, or the sensors already built into HomeView, HomePod, and HomePod mini.
Both thermostats and temperature and humidity sensors are Matter compatible and DIY-friendly, and work with a broad range of HVAC systems, with on-device wire detection to simplify installation.

Every product across the new lineup shares a consistent, seamless setup and control experience. Starting with a single tap with iPhone, the accessory is added to Apple Home, similar to setting up HomePod — with no additional app to download and no separate account to create. Every device supports Thread, helping it maintain connectivity even if a Wi-Fi connection drops. Products also automatically update their network credentials if a customer changes their home Wi-Fi, eliminating a common smart home frustration.

The accessories are designed to work together, and users can control every product with Siri. A single “Good Morning” scene can simultaneously adjust the thermostat, tilt an indoor camera down while a user is getting ready, and start music on HomePod. Using on-device intelligence from iPhone or Apple Watch, users can set up Apple Home to recognize key moments throughout the day: As the last user leaves for work, the thermostat adjusts for an empty home, the door locks, and cameras begin monitoring again. Before they arrive home, the thermostat begins adjusting the temperature, and the front door unlocks automatically as they approach.

Privacy is foundational to Apple Home. Camera footage and personal data in the Home app are stored end-to-end encrypted and never accessible to LG Electronics, Schneider Electric, or Apple. Camera footage is securely processed locally on the customer’s own Apple Home hub or in Private Cloud Compute and, for users with iCloud+, stored encrypted in iCloud for 10 days. No one, not even Apple, can access the data.

For customers who prefer to have their smart home accessories professionally installed, Apple Retail now offers third-party installation from ADT for an additional charge, available in the U.S. starting this fall.

The New Products Advance LG's Zero Labor Home Vision Across Indoor and Outdoor Living Spaces LG Electronics and Apple announced the seven smart home accessories for the Apple Home Collection, including indoor and outdoor cameras, a video doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat and temperature sensor. The new products are co-developed by LG Electronics and Apple, and work seamlessly with Apple devices. These products work together seamlessly to help users with their daily routines, including monitoring and protecting their homes while away. NEW YORK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics (LG) today announced a range of smart home accessories co-developed with Apple for the Apple Home Collection, including indoor and outdoor cameras, and a video doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat and temperature sensor. The new products are designed to make the everyday home experience simpler, more reliable and seamlessly connected and private in Apple Home. These smart home accessories represent LG's commitment to creating connected and adaptive experiences. They also advance the company's ambition to simplify everyday living by reducing the need for manual intervention and enabling more intuitive interactions between customers and their environments. "Creating a truly connected home requires products that work seamlessly together," said Kihyun Jung, head of the Platform Business Center at the LG Home Appliance Solution Company. "By bringing LG's expertise in home appliances and the home environment together with the Apple Home, we are creating intuitive, integrated experiences that fit naturally into customers' daily lives." "Apple has always focused on making products and experiences that are seamless and intuitive, and protect our users' privacy — and that matters more than ever in the home," said Matthew Costello, Apple's vice president of Hardware Engineering. "Combining our hardware and software expertise with LG's deep understanding of the home and connected living lets us build smart home experiences that are simpler to set up, are easier to control, and work effortlessly." Moving Beyond Connectivity to Co-Develop Products and User Experiences Moving beyond just device compatibility, Apple and LG developed these new products together from the early product planning stage, collaborating on hardware, software and user experiences. Each product is designed with a consistent user experience in mind to streamline setup and control. Rather than simply linking individual products through a platform, the accessories are designed to work together. Using the Home app or Siri to control a single "Good Morning" scene can simultaneously adjust the thermostat and tilt an indoor camera down while a user is getting ready.1 And each accessory is encrypted end-to-end in Apple Home, so only users and the people they choose can access their home data. Introducing New Indoor and Outdoor Cameras, a Video Doorbell, Smart Lock, Thermostat and Temperature Sensor Starting in December, with select accessories coming early next year, LG and Apple are launching the full lineup in the United States and Canada, including indoor and outdoor cameras, a video doorbell, a smart lock, a thermostat and a temperature sensor with support for Apple Home and LG ThinQ apps.1 In the United Kingdom, indoor and outdoor cameras and a video doorbell will be available starting December.2 Cameras LG's new indoor and outdoor cameras deliver clear imaging, intelligent detection and privacy-focused controls to help users monitor what matters around their homes. With up to 2.5K video resolution, low-light color night vision, and wide-angle coverage, the cameras provide clear views during the day and at night. Using intelligence, each camera recognizes people, pets, vehicles and motion, helping deliver more relevant alerts and reducing unnecessary notifications. Users can also block selected areas from view and recording, while built-in local storage provides greater control over how recorded footage is stored and reviewed. LG Indoor Cam Plug-In : A wide 160° field of view captures more of the room in a single frame, while a privacy tilt mechanism and physical controls provide a visible and intuitive way to control monitoring when it is not needed. LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In : The camera provides reliable outdoor monitoring with low light color night vision, and 2.5K resolution, helping users maintain a clear view around the home day and night. LG Floodlight Cam : The camera adds dual adaptive floodlights that automatically illuminate the surrounding area when activity is detected, combining outdoor monitoring and lighting in one integrated home security solution. LG Video Doorbell Wired LG Video Doorbell Wired brings clear visibility, more relevant alerts and everyday convenience to the front door. Its dual-camera system combines a 2.5K front camera and a Full HD bottom camera, capturing separate views of visitors, packages and key areas around the entryway for broader coverage. It can also identify people, vehicles, pets and packages and play a helpful chime through Apple HomeView, HomePod or HomePod mini. Low-light color night vision and two-way talk also help users see and respond to activity at their door. LG Smart Deadbolt Lock LG Smart Deadbolt Lock combines smart access, minimal design and everyday convenience, led by hands-free unlocking with home key on a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch and advanced Ultra-Wideband technology. The lock recognizes an authorized user's location and movement to support reliable hands-free entry. NFC tap, PIN code and a physical key provide additional ways to unlock the door, while built-in door sensing and real-time app notifications help users monitor door status and security events. LG Smart Thermostat and LG Temperature Sensor LG Smart Thermostat combines energy efficiency, intuitive design to make home comfort more adaptive and efficient. Adaptive Temperature from Apple can adjust heating and cooling based on headed home, away from home or sleeping. When paired with optional LG Temperature Sensor devices placed in other rooms, the system can monitor temperature and humidity across multiple spaces to support more consistent comfort throughout the home. Advanced sensing algorithms are designed to reduce measurement errors and detect indoor temperature changes in real time, while Matter over Thread enables low-power, responsive connectivity with fewer connection delays and offline disruptions. In the U.S., Clean Energy Guidance from Apple can help optimize energy use based on grid carbon intensity. Through supported utility-provider integrations, LG Smart Thermostat can also shift operation toward lower-cost periods. Privacy in Apple Home Privacy is foundational to Apple Home. Camera footage and personal data in the Home app is stored end-to-end encrypted and never accessible to LG or Apple. 1 Use of the new IoT products requires an Apple home hub, like HomePod, HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K or Apple HomeView. The new IoT products, the LG ThinQ, and the Apple Home require a Wi-Fi connection. Available services, features and compatibility may vary depending on product model, region and country. 2 Product availability, including availability at retail stores, may vary by region and country. LG Electronics is a global innovator in technology and consumer electronics with a presence in almost every country and an international workforce of more than 75,000. LG's four Companies – Home Appliance Solution, Media Entertainment Solution, Vehicle Solution and the Eco Solution – combined for global revenue of over KRW 89 trillion in 2025. LG is a leading manufacturer of consumer and commercial products ranging from TVs, home appliances, air solutions, monitors, automotive components and solutions, and its premium LG SIGNATURE and intelligent LG ThinQ brands are familiar names the world over. Visit www.lg.com/global/newsroom for the latest news.

In the contiguous U.S., Clean Energy Guidance can shift heating and cooling to cleaner, lower-cost periods for users with a compatible utility plan, and the Home app displays usage insights over time, including peak and off-peak rate information. The new thermostats can read temperature and humidity across multiple rooms using LG Electronics’ and Schneider Electric’s new standalone temperature and humidity sensors, or the sensors already built into HomeView, HomePod, and HomePod mini.
Both thermostats and temperature and humidity sensors are Matter compatible and DIY-friendly, and work with a broad range of HVAC systems, with on-device wire detection to simplify installation.

Every product across the new lineup shares a consistent, seamless setup and control experience. Starting with a single tap with iPhone, the accessory is added to Apple Home, similar to setting up HomePod — with no additional app to download and no separate account to create. Every device supports Thread, helping it maintain connectivity even if a Wi-Fi connection drops. Products also automatically update their network credentials if a customer changes their home Wi-Fi, eliminating a common smart home frustration.

The accessories are designed to work together, and users can control every product with Siri. A single “Good Morning” scene can simultaneously adjust the thermostat, tilt an indoor camera down while a user is getting ready, and start music on HomePod. Using on-device intelligence from iPhone or Apple Watch, users can set up Apple Home to recognize key moments throughout the day: As the last user leaves for work, the thermostat adjusts for an empty home, the door locks, and cameras begin monitoring again. Before they arrive home, the thermostat begins adjusting the temperature, and the front door unlocks automatically as they approach.

Privacy is foundational to Apple Home. Camera footage and personal data in the Home app are stored end-to-end encrypted and never accessible to LG Electronics, Schneider Electric, or Apple. Camera footage is securely processed locally on the customer’s own Apple Home hub or in Private Cloud Compute and, for users with iCloud+, stored encrypted in iCloud® for 10 days. No one, not even Apple, can access the data.

A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric.

If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen.
There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning.
Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari.
So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView.
And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that.
HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access.

It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen. HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more. The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad. The centerpiece of the HomeView is a 7-inch square Liquid Retina display. To me, it looks like an enlarged Apple Watch, and the tabletop version with a base comes in Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink and Space Gray colors. This model has a base that contains a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators to bolster the audio performance of the two full-range drivers in the display. Connecting the screen and base together is a stainless steel hinge that allows you to adjust the viewing angle. If you prefer a wall-mounted option, Apple offers the HomeView without a base, but the overall functionality is the same. Interestingly, there are no buttons on the HomeView; the touchscreen display and your voice are the two ways to interact with the device. The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device. That second number is particularly important in the home, for early mornings or if you plan to place the HomeView on your nightstand. The smart display's main, passive screens are called Faces, which are customizable with things like art, photos and various clock designs. Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface. At the top of the display, there's a 12-megapixel FaceTime camera with Center Stage for video calls. Like the Echo Show and other smart displays, HomeView is certainly equipped for catching up with friends and family in a way you can see them. Additionally, the device supports voice and video apps, on top of native iOS apps like Calendar and Weather. HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access. And like Apple's HomePod speakers , you can handoff things like audio or even recipes from your iPhone by holding your handset close to the HomeView. Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari. So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView. And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that. To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information. The speaker also uses facial and voice recognition to distinguish between users, displaying a personalized interface and list of apps based on who is standing in front of the device. If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen. HomeView will also require you to periodically unlock your iPhone or iPad in order to use it, which you'll probably be doing constantly throughout the day anyway. There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning. A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric. The former worked with Apple on indoor and outdoor cameras along with a video doorbell, door lock and thermostat. The Schneider Electric collaboration is an additional option for a thermostat. Apple hasn't said when its Home Collection will be available, but it has released pricing on all of the devices, which range from $199-$349. These devices will also be easily discoverable by your iPhone, where you'll see a card like you would for setting up AirPods when you bring your phone near them. And as you might expect, you can control them all on HomeView and get live video feeds on the smart display. Both versions of the HomeView can be pre-ordered today with general availability scheduled for November 13.

passages: Apple today officially unveiled its new HomeView smart display.
HomeView features a 7-inch square display and comes in two versions: one with a speaker base and another for wall mounting.
The table-top version of HomeView is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.
You can pre-order both today for $299 , with availability beginning November 13.
It will start arriving to customers on November 13.
What do you think of Apple’s new HomeView?
It can also dim to 0.3 nits, making it great for a nightstand.
For audio quality, Apple says HomeView has a “custom-engineered acoustic system” with two full-range drivers in the display, plus a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators.
Apple says the HomeView interface will intelligently adjust based on how far away you are.
It will show “simpler information that’s viewable from across the room” as well as “richer detail” as you step closer.
HomeView can also recognize up to six different people and deliver a “personalized experience” for each one.

This includes a personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. “Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests,” Apple says.
HomeView (Wall Mounted) will be available with a choice of three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home.

Power Mount USB‑C Wall Connector, available starting at $59.95 (U.S.), and Power Mount AC Wired, available starting at $79.95 (U.S.), can be ordered starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app.
There is a collection of “playful and informative” faces for HomeView:
The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background.
Apple says that users with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad can tap into personal context.
Check out 9to5Mac on YouTube for more Apple news:

passages: The HomeView is a 7-inch smart display and speaker that aims to be a central access point for up to six members of a family to access and control Apple’s ecosystem of devices, apps, and the Siri generative AI chatbot that’s currently in beta.
You can also set the screen to automatically adjust its brightness level based on how bright the room is.
Apple started taking preorders for HomeView today.

“With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door.
With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it,” Apple’s announcement said.

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made.
Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”
Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets.
Apple said that Siri requests can run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, where “data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.”

coreStoryFacts.text: It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen.
HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more.
The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad.
A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric.
The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device.
Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface.
To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information.
If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen.
There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning.
Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari.
So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView.
And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that.
HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access.
Apple today officially unveiled its new HomeView smart display.
HomeView features a 7-inch square display and comes in two versions: one with a speaker base and another for wall mounting.
The table-top version of HomeView is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.
You can pre-order both today for $299 , with availability beginning November 13.
It will start arriving to customers on November 13.
What do you think of Apple’s new HomeView?
It can also dim to 0.3 nits, making it great for a nightstand.
For audio quality, Apple says HomeView has a “custom-engineered acoustic system” with two full-range drivers in the display, plus a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators.
Apple says the HomeView interface will intelligently adjust based on how far away you are.
It will show “simpler information that’s viewable from across the room” as well as “richer detail” as you step closer.
HomeView can also recognize up to six different people and deliver a “personalized experience” for each one.

HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more. The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad. The centerpiece of the HomeView is a 7-inch square Liquid Retina display. To me, it looks like an enlarged Apple Watch, and the tabletop version with a base comes in Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink and Space Gray colors. This model has a base that contains a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators to bolster the audio performance of the two full-range drivers in the display. Connecting the screen and base together is a stainless steel hinge that allows you to adjust the viewing angle. If you prefer a wall-mounted option, Apple offers the HomeView without a base, but the overall functionality is the same. Interestingly, there are no buttons on the HomeView; the touchscreen display and your voice are the two ways to interact with the device. The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device. That second number is particularly important in the home, for early mornings or if you plan to place the HomeView on your nightstand. The smart display's main, passive screens are called Faces, which are customizable with things like art, photos and various clock designs. Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface. At the top of the display, there's a 12-megapixel FaceTime camera with Center Stage for video calls. Like the Echo Show and other smart displays, HomeView is certainly equipped for catching up with friends and family in a way you can see them. Additionally, the device supports voice and video apps, on top of native iOS apps like Calendar and Weather. HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access. And like Apple's HomePod speakers , you can handoff things like audio or even recipes from your iPhone by holding your handset close to the HomeView. Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari. So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView. And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that. To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information. The speaker also uses facial and voice recognition to distinguish between users, displaying a personalized interface and list of apps based on who is standing in front of the device. If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen. HomeView will also require you to periodically unlock your iPhone or iPad in order to use it, which you'll probably be doing constantly throughout the day anyway. There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning. A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric. The former worked with Apple on indoor and outdoor cameras along with a video doorbell, door lock and thermostat. The Schneider Electric collaboration is an additional option for a thermostat. Apple hasn't said when its Home Collection will be available, but it has released pricing on all of the devices, which range from $199-$349. These devices will also be easily discoverable by your iPhone, where you'll see a card like you would for setting up AirPods when you bring your phone near them. And as you might expect, you can control them all on HomeView and get live video feeds on the smart display. Both versions of the HomeView can be pre-ordered today with general availability scheduled for November 13.

facts.text: It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen.
HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more.
The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad.
A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric.
The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device.
Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface.
To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information.
If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen.
There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning.
Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari.
So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView.
And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that.
HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access.
Apple today officially unveiled its new HomeView smart display.
HomeView features a 7-inch square display and comes in two versions: one with a speaker base and another for wall mounting.
The table-top version of HomeView is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.
You can pre-order both today for $299 , with availability beginning November 13.
It will start arriving to customers on November 13.

It can also dim to 0.3 nits, making it great for a nightstand.
For audio quality, Apple says HomeView has a “custom-engineered acoustic system” with two full-range drivers in the display, plus a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators.
Apple says the HomeView interface will intelligently adjust based on how far away you are.
It will show “simpler information that’s viewable from across the room” as well as “richer detail” as you step closer.
HomeView can also recognize up to six different people and deliver a “personalized experience” for each one.

This includes a personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. “Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests,” Apple says.
HomeView (Wall Mounted) will be available with a choice of three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home.

Power Mount USB‑C Wall Connector, available starting at $59.95 (U.S.), and Power Mount AC Wired, available starting at $79.95 (U.S.), can be ordered starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app.

The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background.
Apple says that users with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad can tap into personal context.

The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad.
A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric.
The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device.
Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface.
To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information.
If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen.
There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning.
Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari.
So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView.
And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that.
HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access.

extraction.body: Kelly Clarkson reignited a public dispute with Brooklyn novelty store Art of Play after the business challenged her account of an uncomfortable shopping experience. The disagreement has escalated beyond the singer and television personality's original post, with both sides publicly disputing what was said during the encounter. The clash has drawn attention to Art of Play and exposed the impact celebrity criticism can have on small businesses . Newsweek reached out to Clarkson and Art of Play via email for comment on Monday outside regular office hours. The dispute began after Clarkson compared her experience at Art of Play to the famous "Big mistake. Huge" shopping scene from Pretty Woman , where Julia Roberts' character is dismissed by store staff based on assumptions about her spending power. Since then, millions of people have viewed the singer's criticism, prompting the Brooklyn business to issue multiple public responses defending its version of events. On Saturday, Clarkson posted on X that she had traveled to Brooklyn specifically to visit the store after spotting some "really rad" items she wanted to buy. According to the singer, a staff member suggested finding her something "comparable" rather than showing her the products she was interested in. Clarkson said she felt she was treated as if she could not afford the merchandise and compared the experience to Pretty Woman . "You just lost a huge sale," she wrote, while encouraging followers to visit the store if they enjoyed being treated like Roberts' character in the movie. The store said the discussion centered on "Molly," a singing and dancing bird automaton that serves as a fixture in its magic shows. Staff said the bird is permanently attached to the wall and is not available for purchase. While expressing sympathy for anyone who has ever felt judged while shopping, Art of Play said it welcomes visitors regardless of whether they spend money and invites customers to interact with its games, toys and puzzles. The business also said it was shocked to become the target of criticism from millions of people who had never visited the shop after being mentioned by a celebrity. The 2002 American Idol winner said a price tag displaying $15,000 was visible near the bird and alleged a staff member told her that the item could be purchased for that amount. Clarkson claimed she was then offered the option of finding something comparable and said the exchange left her feeling patronized. "You're not only rude, you're also a liar," she wrote. Clarkson added that she regularly supports small businesses and argued that their size should not exempt them from criticism if customers are treated poorly. On Monday, Art of Play issued another statement on Instagram , adding fresh details to its account. The store said Clarkson spent about five minutes inside and asked about Molly. According to Art of Play, staff explained that an almost identical bird is owned by Seattle-based artist Bliss Kolb, who would be willing to sell the twin automaton for $15,000. The business said this was the figure discussed during the visit, not the bird mounted on its wall. After Art of Play shared a statement in response on Sunday, writing that the bird is “permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale” and “plays an important role in the magic shows we host here,” a skeptical Clarkson responded once again , describing the interaction now seen on video and writing: “Cool, cool.

While some are staunchly pro-Clarkson in the debate that has since taken over the internet, others have questioned the singer’s motives for calling out the small business across her social media accounts.

In an interview with Inside Edition on Tuesday, store owner Adam Rubin said that his store has been review-bombed since Clarkson took to social media and named the store, and employees and surrounding businesses have been harassed. “We are afraid for the safety of our shopkeepers.
Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger… Things changed when she used her platform to attack us.
It’s just social warfare,” he said.
Rubin also offered an explanation for why Clarkson might have felt she received subpar treatment: “When Kelly came in, the shop was crowded.
We treated her like a normal person, but apparently that did not live up to her expectations.”
At this point in the footage, Clarkson and the employee part ways as he begins helping other customers in the store.

From footage from an alternative camera angle, we can see Clarkson then find herself standing in front of the automaton bird, where she then gets the attention of a store employee, who can be seen speaking with the musician and pointing at something by the bird, though it is not clear from the video what he was pointing at.

extraction.body: Footage of Kelly Clarkson visiting the Brooklyn novelty store she slammed on Saturday has now been acquired and released by Pablo Torre, the host and executive editor of the investigative podcast, “Pablo Torre Finds Out.” The video offers another perspective to the ongoing drama between Clarkson and Art of Play, the Brooklyn local business she alleged gave her the “Pretty Woman” treatment when an employee looked at the singer as though she “couldn’t afford” Molly, the $15,000 bird automaton she inquired about purchasing. “Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” Clarkson wrote on X before naming the store. Related Stories Reese Witherspoon and Mediawan Partner to Buy Back Hello Sunshine from Candle Media Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat Inks Vertical Series Deal With Fox Entertainment Clarkson can be seen wearing a baseball hat, bright yellow T-shirt, baggy jeans and a backpack in the video. She enters the store, accompanied by her children, and browses and picks up a few items as more shoppers continue to enter. From footage from an alternative camera angle, we can see Clarkson then find herself standing in front of the automaton bird, where she then gets the attention of a store employee, who can be seen speaking with the musician and pointing at something by the bird, though it is not clear from the video what he was pointing at. Popular on Variety After Art of Play shared a statement in response on Sunday, writing that the bird is “permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale” and “plays an important role in the magic shows we host here,” a skeptical Clarkson responded once again , describing the interaction now seen on video and writing: “Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn’t for sale. That’s the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with 👍 so the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn’t happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone ‘yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can.’” At this point in the footage, Clarkson and the employee part ways as he begins helping other customers in the store. Clarkson then puts back the items she was holding, but before she leaves, she turns around and speaks to another employee behind the counter, gesticulating, seemingly upset about the earlier interaction. Other shoppers in the store can be seen looking back at Clarkson, whose entire visit to the store lasted less than five minutes. Her first tweet about the interaction was posted 15 minutes after she left. While some are staunchly pro-Clarkson in the debate that has since taken over the internet, others have questioned the singer’s motives for calling out the small business across her social media accounts. In an interview with Inside Edition on Tuesday, store owner Adam Rubin said that his store has been review-bombed since Clarkson took to social media and named the store, and employees and surrounding businesses have been harassed. “We are afraid for the safety of our shopkeepers. Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger… Things changed when she used her platform to attack us. It’s just social warfare,” he said. Rubin also offered an explanation for why Clarkson might have felt she received subpar treatment: “When Kelly came in, the shop was crowded. She was dressed like everybody else in the shop. We treated her like a normal person, but apparently that did not live up to her expectations.” Art of Play is described as a specialty curiosity shop and online retailer.

extraction.body: Clarkson fans are going to want to look away from a moment like this. Pablo Torre promised us security footage from Kelly Clarkson’s now-viral visit to Art of Play in Brooklyn. Well, we did get the video on Tuesday night, but no audio — bummer. The OG American Idol was in the toy store for exactly four minutes, 50 seconds. What we could see of the brief visit does not bode well for the “Stronger (What Doesn’t Kill You)” singer. For most of her time in the shop, Clarkson can be seen playing around with what appears to be a kaleidoscope near the shop’s entrance. Her interaction with the Art of Play owner was relatively brief. She does appear to inquire with the shop owner about “Molly,” the automaton bird mounted to the wall. After a short conversation, Clarkson walks away from the man to another part of the shop. The store owner appears to attempt to regain her attention, pointing to what appears to be another product on an adjacent wall. She does not appear to respond, and the Art of Play owner moves on to assist another customer. Related Stories Lifestyle New York Store Says Kelly Clarkson Spent "5 Minutes" Inside, Reached Out to "Clear the Air" Amid Star's 'Pretty Woman' Claims Lifestyle Kelly Clarkson Responds After New York Store Denies She Got the 'Pretty Woman' Treatment: "You're a Liar" On her way out of the store, Clarkson appears to share strong feelings toward a second man, who is working the cash register. She’d share those same strong feelings on social media exactly 15 minutes after her exit. “Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me,” Miss Independent wrote. “Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale. But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman . For sure, check it out 👎” The “comparable” product was a pair of other automaton birds made by a German clockmaker. It cost $2,000. Torre purchased it, unveiled it on his show, and said he would auction it off. In response to Clarkson’s initial post, The Art of Play owner said his “small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store.” “Yesterday, Kelly Clarkson visited us in Brooklyn and inquired about buying ‘Molly,’ a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here,” Art of Play posted. “Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale. However, the negative experience Kelly described on Twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop. “At Art of Play whether someone comes in to make a purchase or simply look around for a while, they are equally welcome. We greet everyone who walks in the door with the invitation to ‘pick things up and play.’ And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys.” Clarkson and Art of Play (and the rest of X, fka Twitter) went back and forth from there, which led Torre to take up the cause.

passages: Footage of Kelly Clarkson visiting the Brooklyn novelty store she slammed on Saturday has now been acquired and released by Pablo Torre, the host and executive editor of the investigative podcast, “Pablo Torre Finds Out.”

After Art of Play shared a statement in response on Sunday, writing that the bird is “permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale” and “plays an important role in the magic shows we host here,” a skeptical Clarkson responded once again , describing the interaction now seen on video and writing: “Cool, cool.

While some are staunchly pro-Clarkson in the debate that has since taken over the internet, others have questioned the singer’s motives for calling out the small business across her social media accounts.

In an interview with Inside Edition on Tuesday, store owner Adam Rubin said that his store has been review-bombed since Clarkson took to social media and named the store, and employees and surrounding businesses have been harassed. “We are afraid for the safety of our shopkeepers.
Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger… Things changed when she used her platform to attack us.
It’s just social warfare,” he said.
Rubin also offered an explanation for why Clarkson might have felt she received subpar treatment: “When Kelly came in, the shop was crowded.
We treated her like a normal person, but apparently that did not live up to her expectations.”
At this point in the footage, Clarkson and the employee part ways as he begins helping other customers in the store.

From footage from an alternative camera angle, we can see Clarkson then find herself standing in front of the automaton bird, where she then gets the attention of a store employee, who can be seen speaking with the musician and pointing at something by the bird, though it is not clear from the video what he was pointing at.

extraction.body: An OpenAI employee was arrested after a " sophisticated recording device " was discovered inside its executive conference room, according to the Department of Justice and a post by the company. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, who is a national of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, was arrested on Oct. 9 in connection with the matter, the DOJ said in a release on Tuesday. The company said an employee planted the device a few days before it was found, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation "moved quickly to make an arrest," the post said. The employee was terminated. FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology." Alfozan is also listed as a partner at Raed Ventures , a venture capital firm that focuses on the Middle East and North Africa, according to its website. The firm announced on Feb. 6, 2025, that H.H. Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, a member of the Saudi royal family, had joined the firm as a venture partner. Alfozan was announced as a venture partner two days later. The Raed announcement for Alfozan lists Meta , Microsoft and SAP as previous roles and said he studied computer science and engineering at MIT. Raed, which is headquartered in the Saudi capital of Riyadh, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," OpenAI said in the post. "We take protecting our technology, data and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance." Alfozan was not authorized to access the executive conference room where the device was found, according to the DOJ. The department said footage showed him near the conference room on multiple days before the device was discovered. The DOJ said that on Oct. 5, he went into the room. The DOJ said a bag was also found in the OpenAI building on or about Oct. 5 that belonged to Alfozan. Inside the bag, security found his wallet, ID and another recording device similar to the one that was in the executive conference room. The department said a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse that "shared multiple identifiers and attributes with Alfozan's own chatbot account" was used to get information about continuous audio recording and Wi-Fi. The DOJ said promps were submitted related to "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device." The device was concealed in toilet paper, and its contents were encrypted, according to the DOJ. This security incident comes as the ChatGPT-maker, along with competitors like Anthropic and other big tech names, faces heightened scrutiny over safety protocols after a series of cyber incidents where autonomous agents escaped testing environments and hacked into outside systems. Last week, OpenAI defended its decision to fire three safety researchers, alleging a "significant breach of trust," saying that the researchers "violated clear policies on handling sensitive information." Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni raised safety concerns in a letter to OpenAI's leadership, saying that communications around their exits "have made our former colleagues afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI." —CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this article. OpenAI’s spokesperson, Nate Evans, confirmed that the employee started with the AI model maker in July 2025 and worked on the product team. Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said Alfozan was charged with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications — effectively accusing him of covertly recording people’s voice audio without their permission. Prosecutors said OpenAI caught the device after it was inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in OpenAI’s San Francisco office. Per the prosecutors, Alfozan was caught looking behind the television where the recording device was placed, and where OpenAI had placed a camera that allegedly caught the employee. It’s not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to “capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology.” Neither Alfozan nor his attorney could be immediately reached for comment. He faces five years in prison if convicted. When reached, a spokesperson for the FBI reiterated a statement made by Patel. “Protecting American SI innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation’s economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities,” Patel said.

A specialized OpenAI security team—the technical surveillance countermeasures team—first found a recording device on Sept. 30 during a sweep of the conference room, OpenAI told Fortune . The listening device was plugged into a USB port on the back of a television, concealed by a small piece of toilet paper, according to the FBI. OpenAI contacted the FBI after discovering the listening device, which the company says was sophisticated and designed to evade detection. It had advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring. In that conference room, executives frequently held “discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information,” the FBI said. That includes “proprietary research, product plans, and business-development opportunities, as well as nonpublic information about OpenAI’s technical progress and strategic decisions, capabilities, priorities, government engagements, and commercial relationships.” The suspect is Abdurahman Alfozan, 35, a citizen of Saudi Arabia, the FBI said, without specifying the nature of his status as a U.S. resident. He was an engineering lead, according to his LinkedIn, who worked on OpenAI’s “Agents Platform,” according to his X bio. He formerly worked at Meta for five years, and is a graduate of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (2016) and UC Berkeley (2025). The FBI did not immediately arrest Alfozan upon learning of the device, nor did OpenAI immediately fire him, both of which eventually happened on Oct. 9. He is currently in federal custody and appeared in federal court today, and will appear again on Oct. 19 for a detention hearing. He faces a maximum sentence of 5 years in prison, plus three years supervised release, if convicted. Between Sept. 30 and Oct. 9, OpenAI worked with the FBI on the timing of Alfozan’s termination, so as to not disrupt their investigation, the company said. OpenAI said it restricted Alfozan’s access to systems and parts of the office, suspended his network access, placed him on leave, and took his company-issued equipment. However, there was clearly a continued breakdown in security, as Alfozan was allegedly able to enter the conference room again on Oct. 5. He checked behind the TV for the device, which was no longer there, but was captured on closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage inside OpenAI’s office, according to the FBI. Also “on or about” Oct. 5, Alfozan allegedly left an unattended bag in a different room at OpenAI, which contained his wallet, identification, and another similar recording device. The device pictured in the FBI’s release bears the brand “seeed studio” from seeedstudio.com. It’s unclear what Alfozan planned to do with the data, and at this time neither OpenAI nor the FBI has found evidence that anything leaked. A few days before implanting the device, from Sept. 24 to Sept. 30, Alfozan began consulting an unnamed chatbot, using his spouse’s account, about building, installing, and encrypting audio recordings, among other things, the FBI claimed. He also used a “productivity tool”—presumably internal to OpenAI—to inquire aboutOpenAI’s “building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars, and locations of ‘leadership and exec’ and external partner meetings, according to the FBI. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” OpenAI said in a post on X on Tuesday. “We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance.” However, the investigation remains ongoing. A specialized OpenAI security team—the technical surveillance countermeasures team—first found a recording device on Sept. 30 during a sweep of the conference room, OpenAI told Fortune . The listening device was plugged into a USB port on the back of a television, concealed by a small piece of toilet paper, according to the FBI.

OpenAI contacted the FBI after discovering the listening device, which the company says was sophisticated and designed to evade detection. It had advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring.

In that conference room, executives frequently held “discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information,” the FBI said. That includes “proprietary research, product plans, and business-development opportunities, as well as nonpublic information about OpenAI’s technical progress and strategic decisions, capabilities, priorities, government engagements, and commercial relationships.”

He was an engineering lead, according to his LinkedIn, who worked on OpenAI’s “Agents Platform,” according to his X bio. He formerly worked at Meta for five years, and is a graduate of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (2016) and UC Berkeley (2025).

He is currently in federal custody and appeared in federal court today, and will appear again on Oct. 19 for a detention hearing.
