extraction.body: An OpenAI employee was arrested after a " sophisticated recording device " was discovered inside its executive conference room, according to the Department of Justice and a post by the company. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, who is a national of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, was arrested on Oct. 9 in connection with the matter, the DOJ said in a release on Tuesday. The company said an employee planted the device a few days before it was found, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation "moved quickly to make an arrest," the post said. The employee was terminated. FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology." Alfozan is also listed as a partner at Raed Ventures , a venture capital firm that focuses on the Middle East and North Africa, according to its website. The firm announced on Feb. 6, 2025, that H.H. Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, a member of the Saudi royal family, had joined the firm as a venture partner. Alfozan was announced as a venture partner two days later. The Raed announcement for Alfozan lists Meta , Microsoft and SAP as previous roles and said he studied computer science and engineering at MIT. Raed, which is headquartered in the Saudi capital of Riyadh, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," OpenAI said in the post. "We take protecting our technology, data and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance." Alfozan was not authorized to access the executive conference room where the device was found, according to the DOJ. The department said footage showed him near the conference room on multiple days before the device was discovered. The DOJ said that on Oct. 5, he went into the room. The DOJ said a bag was also found in the OpenAI building on or about Oct. 5 that belonged to Alfozan. Inside the bag, security found his wallet, ID and another recording device similar to the one that was in the executive conference room. The department said a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse that "shared multiple identifiers and attributes with Alfozan's own chatbot account" was used to get information about continuous audio recording and Wi-Fi. The DOJ said promps were submitted related to "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device." The device was concealed in toilet paper, and its contents were encrypted, according to the DOJ. This security incident comes as the ChatGPT-maker, along with competitors like Anthropic and other big tech names, faces heightened scrutiny over safety protocols after a series of cyber incidents where autonomous agents escaped testing environments and hacked into outside systems. Last week, OpenAI defended its decision to fire three safety researchers, alleging a "significant breach of trust," saying that the researchers "violated clear policies on handling sensitive information." Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni raised safety concerns in a letter to OpenAI's leadership, saying that communications around their exits "have made our former colleagues afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI." —CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this article. Abdulrahman Alfozan (pictured in a CCTV image), a 35-year-old Saudi Arabian national, was arrested on Friday and appeared in a federal court earlier today, where he was charged with illegally intercepting oral communications, according to a news release by the Department of Justice.

The device was discovered by OpenAI on Sept. 30. It had been inserted into a USB port on the back of a television inside the executive conference room located at one of the company’s offices in San Francisco. OpenAI said its investigations showed that the device had been installed just a couple of days earlier and concealed in toilet paper. They could not ascertain what communications had been recorded, as the device had been encrypted.

“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier,” OpenAI said in a post on X . “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code or customer data.”

An investigation by the FBI revealed that Alfozan had used a productivity tool to learn about OpenAI’s meeting rooms, its calendars and “leadership and exec” locations, according to OpenAI’s official complaint. A chatbot associated with the suspect’s spouse showed that someone had used it to ask questions about installing and remotely accessing a recording device. That account, which shared multiple identifiers and attributes with Alfozan’s own chatbot account, was also prompted for information about continuous audio recording and Wi-Fi.

The DOJ said in its statement that Alfozan, who had worked with OpenAI as an engineer on one of its product teams since July 2025, was spotted by CCTV cameras going close to, and entering the conference room multiple times before the device was found, despite having no authorization to enter that room. It added that meetings within the conference room “frequently involved discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial and strategic information, including proprietary research, product plans and business-development opportunities.”
Following Alfozan’s arrest, company officials discovered a bag belonging to him that contained a second recording device identical to the one found earlier.

extraction.body: An OpenAI engineer was arrested after the company said it discovered a “sophisticated recording device” hidden in one of its offices. The employee was identified as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national. Alfozan is charged with using or endeavoring to use a device to intercept oral communications, according to a press release from the Department of Justice. Alfozan didn’t have access to this room, but CCTV footage allegedly showed him “near the executive conference room on multiple dates prior to the device’s discovery,” according to the DOJ. Additionally, the DOJ claims OpenAI security discovered a bag Alfozan left in another room inside the company’s office, where they found his wallet, ID, and another recording device. OpenAI says it fired the employee and referred the incident to the FBI. Alfozan was arrested Friday and has remained in custody since, appearing in federal court for the first time on Tuesday. > We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices. We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work. > At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated. > We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance. Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.

extraction.body: Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private. These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator. The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android. Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use. These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android. Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up. “That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.” In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store. And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews. Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates. Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator.

The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.
Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use.

extraction.body: Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store. The new feature from Google makes it easier for people to turn everyday needs into custom applications, even without traditional programming skills. Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices. Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account. Initially, the feature is rolling out to adults aged 18 and older in the United States and select markets. These apps will remain private, absent from public Play Store search results and accessible only to their creators. Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly. The update reflects a broader change in software development. As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful. They can be built for one person, one household or a specific problem that existing software does not adequately address. Until now, people experimenting with AI-generated Android applications faced a gap between creating an app and conveniently using it on their own devices. They could build web applications or work through more technical installation processes, but distributing a native Android app through Google Play traditionally required a developer account and additional publishing steps. Google’s new feature simplifies that process. Users can describe an idea to Gemini through Google AI Studio, refine the generated application and launch it for personal use. The potential applications are straightforward. Someone could create a specialised expense tracker that matches their budgeting habits, a personalised workout log or a household organiser tailored to their family. A student could build a revision tool around a particular subject, while a small business owner could experiment with a simple inventory application. These tools do not need to compete with established apps or attract thousands of downloads. Their value comes from solving a specific problem for the person who created them. This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code. It does not eliminate the need to test software or understand its limitations, but it lowers the technical barrier to experimentation. The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution. Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies. Users who want to distribute their creations publicly must move to a professional developer account and pass the platform’s standard trust and safety reviews. This creates a clearer path from experimentation to publication. A personal project can begin as a private tool, be shared with a small group and eventually become a public product if it proves useful. For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods. It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases. The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves. Google is effectively moving beyond the idea that every useful application must first become a conventional public product. However, the distinction between personal and public apps remains important. An app generated for individual use may contain bugs, mishandle information or produce unreliable results. Private distribution does not automatically make software secure or accurate. Users will still need to be cautious about the permissions they grant and the information they enter. Google is also updating how users discover applications and games. Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps. Google is also bringing Play Store app links into Gemini conversations, allowing the assistant to surface relevant applications directly. Together, these changes show how Google is adapting the Play Store for an environment increasingly shaped by AI. The technology is influencing not only how software is built, but also how people find, personalise and use it. The larger opportunity is a shift away from one-size-fits-all software. Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment. AI-generated personal apps could address smaller, more specific needs that commercial developers have little incentive to pursue. Yet creating software cheaply does not guarantee that it will work well. As more people generate applications, testing, maintenance, privacy and security will become increasingly important. Users may be able to create their own solutions, but they will still need ways to recognise when those solutions are unreliable. Google’s new feature is an early step towards that more personal software environment. It does not replace professional development or remove the need for platform oversight. Instead, it makes the space between having an idea and using a working Android app considerably smaller. The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on. If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves. A writer exploring the intersections of innovation, culture and fashion across Africa

sources.title: Google Play now lets you ‘vibe code’ and launch your own personal Android apps
passages: "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play.

Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account.
Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update.

According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required.

Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC.
Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog.
Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse.

However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release.
Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment.

extraction.body: Google is rolling out a massive wave of updates to the Google Play Store today, and the headline feature completely changes how everyday users can build and run software on their devices. According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required. Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update. "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play. Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account. No Developer Account Needed: You don't have to pay registration fees or jump through publishing hoops to get your custom app onto your phone. Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog. Future Sharing: Rolling out today in the U.S. (for users 18+), the feature is currently limited to your own device. However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release. Smarter discovery and Googlebook optimizations Alongside personal app creation, Google is overhauling how you find content across different form factors and inside the store itself: Built for Googlebook & Beyond: The Play Store is adapting better to non-phone screens. On the new Googlebook platform, apps optimized for large screens are now pushed front and center. Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse. Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment. Additionally, "Play in Gemini" is rolling out soon to bring app and game recommendations directly into your Gemini chats. Sports Topic Pages: You can now follow live scores and jump directly into streaming apps for major soccer leagues, including the Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and MLS. "Gamer DNA," 48-hour Sprints, and PC expansions Mobile and PC gaming on Google Play also received a hefty set of community and discovery upgrades: Game Finder & Gamer DNA: Rolling out in the U.S. today, Game Finder analyzes how you play and your stated preferences (mechanics, art styles, genres) to build your "Gamer DNA." It uses this profile alongside data from similar players to recommend titles that actually match your taste, rather than just pushing what is popular. You can also curate and soon share custom "Game Playlists." Sprints & Sidekick: Available globally today, "Sprints" are fast-paced, 48-hour micro-challenges that match you with groups of two to five players. Community Posts: Game detail pages now feature a built-in Q&A forum with automatic language translation so players can help each other out directly in the store. Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC. Google is also expanding free limited-time Game Trials to PC titles. Finally, Google is adding a new Family Link feature that lets parents share a child's general age range directly with apps to ensure age-appropriate experiences without oversharing personal data. Most of these updates, alongside this week's Play Fest points event, are beginning their rollout today. Be sure to check your Play Store app over the next few days to see the new layout and tools in action.

Are you tired of ad overload in free, single-task apps? Or, can you not find an app that fits a weirdly specific need? Now you can make custom apps for your own Android phone, even if you have zero coding experience. One Tuesday, Google announced that anyone with a standard Google account can build personal apps in Google AI Studio. These apps will run on your own device, launched from a private part of Google Play, and won’t be included in the public Play Store. Also: ‘What’s your AI stack?’ The new job interview question you need to answer You’ll be able to share your apps with close family and friends in the coming months, but you don’t have to. If you do share an app you create and it takes off, Google will provide a “pipeline to graduate into a professional developer account,” meaning you’ll be able to share your app globally via the Play Store. To get started, access the tool in Google AI Studio . There is an app creator in AI Studio, but that’s intended for professional developer accounts and requires USB debugging connected to a PC. This new tool works with that same creator, but it lets you install your app on a personal device with a single click and later directly share it instead of utilizing a public Play Store listing. In the tool, you describe what you want in a prompt, and AI does the rest. While the app is under creation, you’ll see options to add features you might have missed. You can make light edits once the app is complete, or you can completely scrap it and start again. There’s no charge to experiment and build an app. Custom Android apps make app development a much more personal and potentially user-friendly experience. It could be a fantastic option for replacing apps on your phone that you only use for a single thing – like a habit tracker, a calculator or converter, or a specific counter or timer. The ability to make an app with AI isn’t new, but the big selling point here is that you can make an app completely for yourself . Also: I used a free, open-source AI tool to build a working app – in two days My wife had surgery recently, and part of her recovery involves an array of specifically timed medicines, supplements, and liquids. She downloaded a simple tracker app to stay on top of things, but the app was loaded with ads to the point it was too frustrating to use. A monthly subscription was offered to nix the ads, but she didn’t want to pay for an app that would only be used for a few months. Searching for similar apps yielded similar results. With Google’s new system, it seems like it would be simple to make a custom app that avoids both the ads and the fees. And even better, you can tailor this app specifically to what you need. Perhaps the best part about this system is that an app you make doesn’t have to be commercially viable, and it doesn’t even have to be an app that anyone else needs. It just has to work for you . The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution.

Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices.
Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account.
Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly.
For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods.
It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases.
Google is also updating how users discover applications and games.
Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps.

Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment.
This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code.
The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on.
If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves.

extraction.body: Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store. The new feature from Google makes it easier for people to turn everyday needs into custom applications, even without traditional programming skills. Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices. Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account. Initially, the feature is rolling out to adults aged 18 and older in the United States and select markets. These apps will remain private, absent from public Play Store search results and accessible only to their creators. Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly. The update reflects a broader change in software development. As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful. They can be built for one person, one household or a specific problem that existing software does not adequately address. Until now, people experimenting with AI-generated Android applications faced a gap between creating an app and conveniently using it on their own devices. They could build web applications or work through more technical installation processes, but distributing a native Android app through Google Play traditionally required a developer account and additional publishing steps. Google’s new feature simplifies that process. Users can describe an idea to Gemini through Google AI Studio, refine the generated application and launch it for personal use. The potential applications are straightforward. Someone could create a specialised expense tracker that matches their budgeting habits, a personalised workout log or a household organiser tailored to their family. A student could build a revision tool around a particular subject, while a small business owner could experiment with a simple inventory application. These tools do not need to compete with established apps or attract thousands of downloads. Their value comes from solving a specific problem for the person who created them. This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code. It does not eliminate the need to test software or understand its limitations, but it lowers the technical barrier to experimentation. The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution. Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies. Users who want to distribute their creations publicly must move to a professional developer account and pass the platform’s standard trust and safety reviews. This creates a clearer path from experimentation to publication. A personal project can begin as a private tool, be shared with a small group and eventually become a public product if it proves useful. For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods. It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases. The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves. Google is effectively moving beyond the idea that every useful application must first become a conventional public product. However, the distinction between personal and public apps remains important. An app generated for individual use may contain bugs, mishandle information or produce unreliable results. Private distribution does not automatically make software secure or accurate. Users will still need to be cautious about the permissions they grant and the information they enter. Google is also updating how users discover applications and games. Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps. Google is also bringing Play Store app links into Gemini conversations, allowing the assistant to surface relevant applications directly. Together, these changes show how Google is adapting the Play Store for an environment increasingly shaped by AI. The technology is influencing not only how software is built, but also how people find, personalise and use it. The larger opportunity is a shift away from one-size-fits-all software. Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment. AI-generated personal apps could address smaller, more specific needs that commercial developers have little incentive to pursue. Yet creating software cheaply does not guarantee that it will work well. As more people generate applications, testing, maintenance, privacy and security will become increasingly important. Users may be able to create their own solutions, but they will still need ways to recognise when those solutions are unreliable. Google’s new feature is an early step towards that more personal software environment. It does not replace professional development or remove the need for platform oversight. Instead, it makes the space between having an idea and using a working Android app considerably smaller. The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on. If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves. A writer exploring the intersections of innovation, culture and fashion across Africa

sources.title: Google Play now lets you ‘vibe code’ and launch your own personal Android apps
passages: "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play.

Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account.
Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update.

According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required.

Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC.
Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog.
Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse.

However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release.
Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment.

extraction.body: Google is rolling out a massive wave of updates to the Google Play Store today, and the headline feature completely changes how everyday users can build and run software on their devices. According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required. Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update. "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play. Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account. No Developer Account Needed: You don't have to pay registration fees or jump through publishing hoops to get your custom app onto your phone. Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog. Future Sharing: Rolling out today in the U.S. (for users 18+), the feature is currently limited to your own device. However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release. Smarter discovery and Googlebook optimizations Alongside personal app creation, Google is overhauling how you find content across different form factors and inside the store itself: Built for Googlebook & Beyond: The Play Store is adapting better to non-phone screens. On the new Googlebook platform, apps optimized for large screens are now pushed front and center. Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse. Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment. Additionally, "Play in Gemini" is rolling out soon to bring app and game recommendations directly into your Gemini chats. Sports Topic Pages: You can now follow live scores and jump directly into streaming apps for major soccer leagues, including the Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and MLS. "Gamer DNA," 48-hour Sprints, and PC expansions Mobile and PC gaming on Google Play also received a hefty set of community and discovery upgrades: Game Finder & Gamer DNA: Rolling out in the U.S. today, Game Finder analyzes how you play and your stated preferences (mechanics, art styles, genres) to build your "Gamer DNA." It uses this profile alongside data from similar players to recommend titles that actually match your taste, rather than just pushing what is popular. You can also curate and soon share custom "Game Playlists." Sprints & Sidekick: Available globally today, "Sprints" are fast-paced, 48-hour micro-challenges that match you with groups of two to five players. Community Posts: Game detail pages now feature a built-in Q&A forum with automatic language translation so players can help each other out directly in the store. Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC. Google is also expanding free limited-time Game Trials to PC titles. Finally, Google is adding a new Family Link feature that lets parents share a child's general age range directly with apps to ensure age-appropriate experiences without oversharing personal data. Most of these updates, alongside this week's Play Fest points event, are beginning their rollout today. Be sure to check your Play Store app over the next few days to see the new layout and tools in action.

facts.text: Are you tired of ad overload in free, single-task apps?

Faraday Future Announces FF EAI Robotics’ Employee Incentive Plan to Allocate Approximately 25% of Its Outstanding Shares for Stock Options for Its Core Team, Aiming to Establish an Industry-First Partnership Model Los Angeles, CA (September 23, 2026) – Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. (“FFR”). FF EAI Robotics is allocating approximately 25% of the capitalization of FF EAI Robotics on a fully diluted basis as the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan to provide long-term equity incentives for the Company’s core management team, key leaders, and key employees. The proposed plan is intended to further strengthen FF’s robotics strategy and help FF EAI Robotics establish a partnership model in the robotics industry. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI. “The equity incentive plan is intended to create a long-term incentive and value-sharing mechanism,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. “By linking the core team’s long-term interests to the growth of our robotics business and enterprise value, we aim to align the interests of our team, the Company and our stockholders. We believe this will encourage a partnership mindset, sustained commitment and long-term value creation.” FF aims to build the world’s only “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World. Its “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem is taking shape, and Robot World 2.0 is complete. Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms. At its 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch, FF launched nine EAI Device configurations across two robot forms, three series and five models: FF All-New Futurist, FF Master Mini, FX Aegis Hyper, FX Aegis Mega and FX Aegis Classic Ultra-W. All nine are now available for sale and delivery. FF also launched four Industry Productivity Solutions for K-12 Education, Research, Security and Inspection. Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy. First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront. Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry. Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector. Through this flywheel, FF seeks to maximize its commercial value and advance the development of Physical AI. Faraday Future Announces FF EAI Robotics’ Employee Incentive Plan to Allocate Approximately 25% of Its Outstanding Shares for Stock Options for Its Core Team, Aiming to Establish an Industry-First Partnership Model

Los Angeles, CA (September 23, 2026) – Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. (“FFR”). FF EAI Robotics is allocating approximately 25% of the capitalization of FF EAI Robotics on a fully diluted basis as the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan to provide long-term equity incentives for the Company’s core management team, key leaders, and key employees. The proposed plan is intended to further strengthen FF’s robotics strategy and help FF EAI Robotics establish a partnership model in the robotics industry. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI.

“The equity incentive plan is intended to create a long-term incentive and value-sharing mechanism,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. “By linking the core team’s long-term interests to the growth of our robotics business and enterprise value, we aim to align the interests of our team, the Company and our stockholders. We believe this will encourage a partnership mindset, sustained commitment and long-term value creation.”

FF aims to build the world’s only “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World. Its “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem is taking shape, and Robot World 2.0 is complete. Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms.

At its 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch, FF launched nine EAI Device configurations across two robot forms, three series and five models: FF All-New Futurist, FF Master Mini, FX Aegis Hyper, FX Aegis Mega and FX Aegis Classic Ultra-W. All nine are now available for sale and delivery. FF also launched four Industry Productivity Solutions for K-12 Education, Research, Security and Inspection.
Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders

FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy.

First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront.

Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry.

Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector.

Founded in 2014, Faraday Future (FF) is a U.S.-based Physical AI ecosystem company dedicated to reshaping the future of robotics and mobility solutions through AI innovation and technologies. FF focuses on two major product strategies within the Embodied AI (EAI) robotics business: EAI humanoid and bionic robots, and EAI automotive-focused robots. By building a “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem comprising the EAI Brain and Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions and the EAI Data Factory, FF aims to create an evolutionary flywheel: scaled device delivery, data collection and training, continuous evolution of the EAI Brain, stronger product capabilities, and even larger-scale delivery and deployment. Through this flywheel, FF seeks to maximize its commercial value and advance the development of Physical AI.

(NASDAQ: FFR ), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company that has proposed to acquire Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc.'s (NASDAQ: FFAI ) EAI Robotics business, today highlighted FFAI's announcement that this week's Investor Weekly Report from Faraday Future ("FF") Founder and Global CEO YT Jia has been rescheduled to October 14.

Additionally, FFR and FFAI will host a joint new product launch event on October 14, 2026, featuring four major launches focused on embodied AI robotics, Physical AI education, and developer enablement.
The event will feature FF Nova, FF's first embodied AI humanoid robot designed for developers and educational institutions, through an exclusive, invitation-only launch.
FFAI has also announced that FF will introduce FF Nova Mini, a humanoid robot designed for foundational Physical AI education, along with the EAI Education Ecosystem Brain and Curriculum Skills 2.0.
In addition, FF will launch the FF Nova Developer Reinforcement Learning Platform and open exclusive early access to the developer community.

FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR ) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI (EAI) robotics company that is in the process of acquiring the FF EAI Robotics business. Upon completion of the acquisition, the Company will focus on the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization, and deployment of intelligent robotic technologies, products, and industry solutions.

The Company is committed to building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of EAI Brain & Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions, and EAI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," the Company aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified EAI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications.

The FF EAI Robotics business has already achieved commercial deliveries of humanoid and biomimetic robotic products. Through its multi-form-factor robotic products, EAI technology platform, closed-loop data capabilities, and industry solutions, the business continues to advance the scaled adoption of robotics across real-world applications. The Company also operates RoboShare, a robot-sharing and services platform designed to connect robotic assets, service capabilities, customer demand, and ecosystem partners, further strengthening its robotics commercialization and service ecosystem.

Faraday Future Announces FF EAI Robotics’ Employee Incentive Plan to Allocate Approximately 25% of Its Outstanding Shares for Stock Options for Its Core Team, Aiming to Establish an Industry-First Partnership Model Los Angeles, CA (September 23, 2026) – Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. (“FFR”). FF EAI Robotics is allocating approximately 25% of the capitalization of FF EAI Robotics on a fully diluted basis as the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan to provide long-term equity incentives for the Company’s core management team, key leaders, and key employees. The proposed plan is intended to further strengthen FF’s robotics strategy and help FF EAI Robotics establish a partnership model in the robotics industry. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI. “The equity incentive plan is intended to create a long-term incentive and value-sharing mechanism,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. “By linking the core team’s long-term interests to the growth of our robotics business and enterprise value, we aim to align the interests of our team, the Company and our stockholders. We believe this will encourage a partnership mindset, sustained commitment and long-term value creation.” FF aims to build the world’s only “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World. Its “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem is taking shape, and Robot World 2.0 is complete. Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms. At its 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch, FF launched nine EAI Device configurations across two robot forms, three series and five models: FF All-New Futurist, FF Master Mini, FX Aegis Hyper, FX Aegis Mega and FX Aegis Classic Ultra-W. All nine are now available for sale and delivery. FF also launched four Industry Productivity Solutions for K-12 Education, Research, Security and Inspection. Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy. First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront. Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry. Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI.

Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms.

extraction.body: Apple on Tuesday announced a home hub called HomeView, marking CEO John Ternus' first launch outside of iPhones since he took over from Tim Cook at the start of September. Apple said the device with a 7-inch screen was designed to be mounted on a wall or placed on a table. It's designed for multiple people in a household, and will recognize the user by their face to display pertinent information. It starts at $299 and ships on Nov. 13. Tuesday's launch event is the second under Ternus, who was the company's longtime hardware boss before being promoted to CEO. Last month, Apple announced new models of its most important product, the iPhone, including a foldable model called the Duo that retails for nearly $2,000. Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday. The new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and has a redesigned remote that can play a sound if it is lost. Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price. The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month. Apple said HomeView features Siri AI, which can answer a broad range of questions. Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad. It has a built-in speaker for playing music. "It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's marketing head Greg Joswiak said in a statement. Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence. It can also be used to make FaceTime calls and as a digital photo frame. It's equipped with an Apple A18 chip. It supports up to six users. Apple TV, HomePods, and HomeView are included in Apple's Wearables, Home, and Accessories category, which reported $7.88 billion in sales in the most recent quarter ended June, which was about 7% of the company's total revenue. The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch. But while Apple has dabbled in home products and platforms in the past, Tuesday's announcement shows Apple is making its home products a higher priority under Ternus. "Apple always waits for an ecosystem to develop first until they are positive they can provide a stellar user experience," said Jennifer Kent, principal analyst at Parks Associates, which conducts research on the connected home. Apple said its new products, including HomeView, can be used as a smart home hub, coordinating notifications and actions in the home and working with a range of products, including new locks, doorbells, and cameras from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. Apple is emphasizing privacy, and said on Tuesday that its Apple Home Collection accessories encrypt data so that only the user and people they share with can see it. Other smart home cameras, for example, maintain limited access to user video, or store it on servers. "They are going above and beyond what a lot of other companies do when it comes to privacy and security protections," Kent said. Apple's integration with the smart home is not just about sales, but also helps further lock customers into its ecosystem. People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone. HomeView can also become a smart home dashboard, Apple said. It can be used to view camera feeds, adjust the thermostat, or lock connected doors around the house. Apple said that setting up a new smart home device takes one tap from the user's iPhone. Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories. But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage. passages: Apple on Tuesday announced a home hub called HomeView, marking CEO John Ternus' first launch outside of iPhones since he took over from Tim Cook at the start of September.

Apple said the device with a 7-inch screen was designed to be mounted on a wall or placed on a table. It's designed for multiple people in a household, and will recognize the user by their face to display pertinent information. It starts at $299 and ships on Nov. 13.

Tuesday's launch event is the second under Ternus, who was the company's longtime hardware boss before being promoted to CEO. Last month, Apple announced new models of its most important product, the iPhone, including a foldable model called the Duo that retails for nearly $2,000.

Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday. The new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and has a redesigned remote that can play a sound if it is lost. Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price.

The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month.

Apple said HomeView features Siri AI, which can answer a broad range of questions. Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad. It has a built-in speaker for playing music.

"It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's marketing head Greg Joswiak said in a statement.

Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence. It can also be used to make FaceTime calls and as a digital photo frame. It's equipped with an Apple A18 chip. It supports up to six users.

Apple TV, HomePods, and HomeView are included in Apple's Wearables, Home, and Accessories category, which reported $7.88 billion in sales in the most recent quarter ended June, which was about 7% of the company's total revenue. The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch.
But while Apple has dabbled in home products and platforms in the past, Tuesday's announcement shows Apple is making its home products a higher priority under Ternus.

"Apple always waits for an ecosystem to develop first until they are positive they can provide a stellar user experience," said Jennifer Kent, principal analyst at Parks Associates, which conducts research on the connected home.

Apple said its new products, including HomeView, can be used as a smart home hub, coordinating notifications and actions in the home and working with a range of products, including new locks, doorbells, and cameras from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

Apple is emphasizing privacy, and said on Tuesday that its Apple Home Collection accessories encrypt data so that only the user and people they share with can see it. Other smart home cameras, for example, maintain limited access to user video, or store it on servers.
"They are going above and beyond what a lot of other companies do when it comes to privacy and security protections," Kent said.

Apple's integration with the smart home is not just about sales, but also helps further lock customers into its ecosystem. People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone.
HomeView can also become a smart home dashboard, Apple said. It can be used to view camera feeds, adjust the thermostat, or lock connected doors around the house.
Apple said that setting up a new smart home device takes one tap from the user's iPhone.

Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories. But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage. It also comes as Ternus has reportedly pushed the company to release products faster.
Apple's new Apple TV 4K got a price hike from $199 to $299, and follows a similar price increase earlier this year, after Cook said that memory costs for Apple were unsustainable.

Pre-orders will begin soon, with sales expected to start on November 13, indicating a growing focus on connected home products.

passages: Apple has opened preorders for HomeView, a $299 smart display intended to sit at the center of a connected household.
The 7-inch device combines touch controls for lights, locks and cameras with FaceTime, speakers, personalized household screens and Siri AI.
13 in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, India and New Zealand.
According to Apple’s HomeView announcement , the device has a 7-inch Liquid Retina display and an A18 chip.
The wall version requires a separate Schneider Home mount.
Apple lists USB-C and AC-wired mounts at $59.95 and $79.95, respectively, while a Power over Ethernet mount priced at $129.95 is not expected until early 2027.
Apple says HomeView will not be sold in the European Union at launch because Siri AI is unavailable in iOS there.
The launch gives Apple a direct answer to screen-equipped home hubs from Amazon and Google, a category where Apple has largely relied on iPads, HomePods and third-party accessories.
Apple also says camera and microphone information is processed in protected hardware runtimes unavailable to HomeView software, apps, users or Apple itself.
Apple is also using HomeView to promote its Apple Home Collection, a group of accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.
CNET’s launch coverage cites Ben Wood, chief analyst at CCS Insight, saying Apple has made setup for the new home products simpler than alternatives that require separate apps and QR-code scanning.
Personal-context Siri requests also require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.
Apple describes HomeView as a shared device for household tasks while keeping personal content tied to a user’s paired device.
HomeView is a touch-and-voice controller for compatible Apple Home and Matter accessories.
Apple says users can view as many as nine live camera feeds at once and control connected devices through the screen or Siri.

extraction.body: Apple has opened preorders for HomeView, a $299 smart display intended to sit at the center of a connected household. The 7-inch device combines touch controls for lights, locks and cameras with FaceTime, speakers, personalized household screens and Siri AI. It goes on sale Nov. 13 in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, India and New Zealand. The launch gives Apple a direct answer to screen-equipped home hubs from Amazon and Google, a category where Apple has largely relied on iPads, HomePods and third-party accessories. Apple says HomeView can recognize up to six people, while its most sensitive personalized functions require an eligible, nearby and recently unlocked iPhone or iPad. According to Apple’s HomeView announcement , the device has a 7-inch Liquid Retina display and an A18 chip. It is available as a tabletop model or a wall-mounted model, both listed at $299 in the United States. The wall version requires a separate Schneider Home mount. Apple lists USB-C and AC-wired mounts at $59.95 and $79.95, respectively, while a Power over Ethernet mount priced at $129.95 is not expected until early 2027. Apple says HomeView can recognize up to six people and show personalized calendars, reminders, photo collections and home controls. CNBC’s launch coverage also describes the device as a showcase for the company’s Siri AI effort and household-profile system. Recognition does not by itself open a person’s private material. Apple says personal content requires that user’s paired iPhone or iPad to be nearby and recently unlocked. Personal-context Siri requests also require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. Apple describes HomeView as a shared device for household tasks while keeping personal content tied to a user’s paired device. Apple also says camera and microphone information is processed in protected hardware runtimes unavailable to HomeView software, apps, users or Apple itself. The company presents those protections as part of its privacy approach. HomeView is a touch-and-voice controller for compatible Apple Home and Matter accessories. Apple says users can view as many as nine live camera feeds at once and control connected devices through the screen or Siri. Apple is also using HomeView to promote its Apple Home Collection, a group of accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. CNET’s launch coverage cites Ben Wood, chief analyst at CCS Insight, saying Apple has made setup for the new home products simpler than alternatives that require separate apps and QR-code scanning. Apple’s announcement says HomeView works with Apple TV and compatible third-party audio and video apps. The release does not provide a service-by-service list or clearly state which video apps run directly on HomeView and which require an iPhone, iPad or another Apple device. WIRED’s hands-on report says HomeView has no App Store and that YouTube, Netflix and Disney+ were not available as native apps at the time of its briefing. AppleInsider reported that video playback may depend on AirPlay from an iPhone or iPad or on CarPlay-related functionality. The available reporting does not resolve which services Apple considers compatible video apps. Preorders began Oct. 13 in the first group of markets. Apple says Singapore preorders begin Oct. 15. South Africa is scheduled to receive HomeView on Nov. 13 through authorized resellers. Apple says HomeView will not be sold in the European Union at launch because Siri AI is unavailable in iOS there. Siri AI is labeled beta in HomeView software version 27.2, and Apple says its personal-context capabilities require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. HomeView becomes available Nov. 13 in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States.

coreStoryFacts.text: Apple said its new products, including HomeView, can be used as a smart home hub, coordinating notifications and actions in the home and working with a range of products, including new locks, doorbells, and cameras from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.
Apple on Tuesday announced a home hub called HomeView, marking CEO John Ternus' first launch outside of iPhones since he took over from Tim Cook at the start of September.
Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad.

"It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's marketing head Greg Joswiak said in a statement.
The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch.

The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month.
Apple is emphasizing privacy, and said on Tuesday that its Apple Home Collection accessories encrypt data so that only the user and people they share with can see it.
Other smart home cameras, for example, maintain limited access to user video, or store it on servers.
Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence.
People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone.

"Apple always waits for an ecosystem to develop first until they are positive they can provide a stellar user experience," said Jennifer Kent, principal analyst at Parks Associates, which conducts research on the connected home.
Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday.
Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price.
Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories.
But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage.
It also comes as Ternus has reportedly pushed the company to release products faster.
Apple launches HomeView, its US$299 smart display with Siri AI and facial recognition
Prices start at $299 with pre-orders opened and shipments starting November 13.
Apple enters the smart screen battle with HomeView: 7 inches, facial recognition, and Siri
HomeView includes a 7-inch Liquid Retina display and a domed speaker base connected by a stainless steel hinge, and HomeView can be placed on a tabletop or wall-mounted.
HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My.
Apple’s first smart display is the 7-inch HomeView for $299
Apple releases HomeView smart home hub with screen as showcase for Siri AI
Apple launches $299 HomeView hub alongside new smart home range

Tuesday's launch event is the second under Ternus, who was the company's longtime hardware boss before being promoted to CEO. Last month, Apple announced new models of its most important product, the iPhone, including a foldable model called the Duo that retails for nearly $2,000. Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday. The new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and has a redesigned remote that can play a sound if it is lost. Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price. The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month. Apple said HomeView features Siri AI, which can answer a broad range of questions. Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad. It has a built-in speaker for playing music. "It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's marketing head Greg Joswiak said in a statement. Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence. It can also be used to make FaceTime calls and as a digital photo frame. It's equipped with an Apple A18 chip. It supports up to six users. Apple TV, HomePods, and HomeView are included in Apple's Wearables, Home, and Accessories category, which reported $7.88 billion in sales in the most recent quarter ended June, which was about 7% of the company's total revenue. The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch. But while Apple has dabbled in home products and platforms in the past, Tuesday's announcement shows Apple is making its home products a higher priority under Ternus. Other smart home cameras, for example, maintain limited access to user video, or store it on servers. "They are going above and beyond what a lot of other companies do when it comes to privacy and security protections," Kent said. Apple's integration with the smart home is not just about sales, but also helps further lock customers into its ecosystem. People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone. HomeView can also become a smart home dashboard, Apple said. It can be used to view camera feeds, adjust the thermostat, or lock connected doors around the house. Apple said that setting up a new smart home device takes one tap from the user's iPhone. Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories. But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage. extraction.body: Apple has opened preorders for HomeView, a $299 smart display intended to sit at the center of a connected household. The 7-inch device combines touch controls for lights, locks and cameras with FaceTime, speakers, personalized household screens and Siri AI. It goes on sale Nov. 13 in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, India and New Zealand. The launch gives Apple a direct answer to screen-equipped home hubs from Amazon and Google, a category where Apple has largely relied on iPads, HomePods and third-party accessories. Apple says HomeView can recognize up to six people, while its most sensitive personalized functions require an eligible, nearby and recently unlocked iPhone or iPad. According to Apple’s HomeView announcement , the device has a 7-inch Liquid Retina display and an A18 chip. It is available as a tabletop model or a wall-mounted model, both listed at $299 in the United States. The wall version requires a separate Schneider Home mount. Apple lists USB-C and AC-wired mounts at $59.95 and $79.95, respectively, while a Power over Ethernet mount priced at $129.95 is not expected until early 2027. Apple says HomeView can recognize up to six people and show personalized calendars, reminders, photo collections and home controls. CNBC’s launch coverage also describes the device as a showcase for the company’s Siri AI effort and household-profile system. Recognition does not by itself open a person’s private material. Apple says personal content requires that user’s paired iPhone or iPad to be nearby and recently unlocked. Personal-context Siri requests also require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. Apple describes HomeView as a shared device for household tasks while keeping personal content tied to a user’s paired device. Apple also says camera and microphone information is processed in protected hardware runtimes unavailable to HomeView software, apps, users or Apple itself. The company presents those protections as part of its privacy approach. HomeView is a touch-and-voice controller for compatible Apple Home and Matter accessories. Apple says users can view as many as nine live camera feeds at once and control connected devices through the screen or Siri. Apple is also using HomeView to promote its Apple Home Collection, a group of accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. CNET’s launch coverage cites Ben Wood, chief analyst at CCS Insight, saying Apple has made setup for the new home products simpler than alternatives that require separate apps and QR-code scanning. Apple’s announcement says HomeView works with Apple TV and compatible third-party audio and video apps. The release does not provide a service-by-service list or clearly state which video apps run directly on HomeView and which require an iPhone, iPad or another Apple device. WIRED’s hands-on report says HomeView has no App Store and that YouTube, Netflix and Disney+ were not available as native apps at the time of its briefing. AppleInsider reported that video playback may depend on AirPlay from an iPhone or iPad or on CarPlay-related functionality. The available reporting does not resolve which services Apple considers compatible video apps. Preorders began Oct. 13 in the first group of markets. Apple says Singapore preorders begin Oct. 15. South Africa is scheduled to receive HomeView on Nov. 13 through authorized resellers. Apple says HomeView will not be sold in the European Union at launch because Siri AI is unavailable in iOS there. Siri AI is labeled beta in HomeView software version 27.2, and Apple says its personal-context capabilities require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. HomeView becomes available Nov. 13 in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States.
