HomeView is a touch-and-voice controller for compatible Apple Home and Matter accessories. Apple says users can view as many as nine live camera feeds at once and control connected devices through the screen or Siri.

Apple is also using HomeView to promote its Apple Home Collection, a group of accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. CNET’s launch coverage cites Ben Wood, chief analyst at CCS Insight, saying Apple has made setup for the new home products simpler than alternatives that require separate apps and QR-code scanning.

Apple’s announcement says HomeView works with Apple TV and compatible third-party audio and video apps. The release does not provide a service-by-service list or clearly state which video apps run directly on HomeView and which require an iPhone, iPad or another Apple device.

WIRED’s hands-on report says HomeView has no App Store and that YouTube, Netflix and Disney+ were not available as native apps at the time of its briefing. AppleInsider reported that video playback may depend on AirPlay from an iPhone or iPad or on CarPlay-related functionality. The available reporting does not resolve which services Apple considers compatible video apps.

Preorders began Oct. 13 in the first group of markets. Apple says Singapore preorders begin Oct. 15. South Africa is scheduled to receive HomeView on Nov. 13 through authorized resellers. Apple says HomeView will not be sold in the European Union at launch because Siri AI is unavailable in iOS there.

Siri AI is labeled beta in HomeView software version 27.2, and Apple says its personal-context capabilities require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. HomeView becomes available Nov. 13 in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States.

passages: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.

And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.
By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.

HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.
With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030.

HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.
HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry.
HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system.
Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple.

To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio.
A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension.
Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds.

extraction.body: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced Apple HomeView , designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core. 1 HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses. 2 Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13. “Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.” HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable. The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer. A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation. A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests. Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer. With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before. 3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro. With Siri AI built into HomeView, even users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery. With powerful new features and unrivaled privacy protections, Siri remains the world’s most private digital assistant. Users can personalize HomeView with a collection of playful and informative faces that display information at a glance, taking full advantage of the vibrant Liquid Retina display. The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background. By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill. The Flow face dynamically responds to physical presence and movement, transforming HomeView into a piece of interactive art. And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments. HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension. Powered by Apple silicon and real-time system sensors, advanced computational audio continuously optimizes loudness and bass response at any volume. The wall-mounted version delivers rich sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement. HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Music, complete with animated album art and lyrics, as well as Apple Podcasts, Apple News, 4 Apple TV, and compatible third-party audio and video apps. 5 With Handoff, users can continue listening to a song they were playing in the car or on a walk by placing their iPhone in front of the HomeView display. By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio. HomeView makes it effortless for users to stay in touch and get things done around the house. FaceTime and Center Stage keep everyone framed perfectly, even when participants are moving around the room. 6 Messages can be read and answered by voice or with the onscreen keyboard. Intercom lets users broadcast a quick message to a single room or the whole house — reaching other HomeView and HomePod speakers, as well as personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. In the kitchen, HomeView is the perfect sous chef, converting recipes from the web into step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking, so users can stay focused on what’s cooking. With Find My, users can check in on loved ones who have shared their locations with them, or track down a misplaced iPhone, AirPods charging case, or personal item with an AirTag attached. And with Live Activities, HomeView surfaces timely, at-a-glance information, like the song that’s currently playing, an active timer, or an incoming Intercom message from another room. Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced Apple HomeView , designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core. 1 HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses. 2

Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13.

“Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable.

The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer.

A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation.
A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home

HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests.
Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence

HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.

With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before. 3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro.

With Siri AI built into HomeView, even users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery.
With powerful new features and unrivaled privacy protections, Siri remains the world’s most private digital assistant.

Users can personalize HomeView with a collection of playful and informative faces that display information at a glance, taking full advantage of the vibrant Liquid Retina display. The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background. By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill. The Flow face dynamically responds to physical presence and movement, transforming HomeView into a piece of interactive art. And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments.

HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension. Powered by Apple silicon and real-time system sensors, advanced computational audio continuously optimizes loudness and bass response at any volume. The wall-mounted version delivers rich sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement.

HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Music, complete with animated album art and lyrics, as well as Apple Podcasts, Apple News, 4 Apple TV, and compatible third-party audio and video apps. 5 With Handoff, users can continue listening to a song they were playing in the car or on a walk by placing their iPhone in front of the HomeView display. By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.

HomeView makes it effortless for users to stay in touch and get things done around the house. FaceTime and Center Stage keep everyone framed perfectly, even when participants are moving around the room. 6 Messages can be read and answered by voice or with the onscreen keyboard. Intercom lets users broadcast a quick message to a single room or the whole house — reaching other HomeView and HomePod speakers, as well as personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. In the kitchen, HomeView is the perfect sous chef, converting recipes from the web into step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking, so users can stay focused on what’s cooking.

With Find My, users can check in on loved ones who have shared their locations with them, or track down a misplaced iPhone, AirPods charging case, or personal item with an AirTag attached. And with Live Activities, HomeView surfaces timely, at-a-glance information, like the song that’s currently playing, an active timer, or an incoming Intercom message from another room.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds. The Home Modular face offers instant access to users’ favorite accessories, while the Home Camera face can livestream up to nine video feeds at once, letting users keep an eye on doorstep deliveries and pets playing in the yard.

With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door. With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it. 7 Offering added peace of mind, HomeView also detects the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms and alerts users on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.

HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories. 8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more. 9

Like every Apple product, HomeView was built with privacy and security at its core. HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system. Isolation features added across many core components of the silicon work in tandem to protect Secure Exclaves and keep them segregated from the rest of the system. Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple. To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked. 10

Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud. When processed in Private Cloud Compute, data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.

HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 11 and designed to be recycled.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple unveiled the HomeView smart display and the Apple Home Collection accessories today, aiming to expand its connected‑home footprint through AI‑powered Siri and partnerships with LG and Schneider Electric. NEW YORK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market. The HomeView device, which starts at $299 and starts shipping next month, is Apple's latest entry into a highly competitive market for connected home devices. It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition and will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own. "Apple needs to demonstrate that its AI capabilities can deliver meaningful benefits beyond basic voice commands, simplifying everyday tasks and bringing greater intelligence to the home," said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore. Investors are looking more closely at Apple's hardware sales for growth. The company's services revenue has come under regulatory pressure, although that could also eventually get a boost from the new suite of devices. "The objective seems to be to drive high-margin 'Services' revenue via Apple TV, Apple Pay and iCloud," said Melissa Otto, head of Visible Alpha Research at S&P Global Market Intelligence, noting that Apple's 2027 services revenue is forecast to rise 12% to $138 billion. "Growth in Apple's lucrative subscription services may be the gateway to earnings growth increases over the next two years." Apple this summer upgraded Siri's capabilities with assistance from Google but analysts said it is unclear whether its AI assistant is competitive enough to lure consumers to a crowded connected home device space. The device features a 7-inch screen — which Apple said is to make it fit into a home without being too imposing — similar to Apple's "sunflower" iMac from the 2000s. And while it features a menu of square app icons like an iPhone or iPad that change depending on which user is recognized, Apple showed it being used more often via voice with its Siri AI assistant. The launches also coincide with growing worries that connected devices, including refrigerators and smart TVs, could be vulnerable to hackers. Apple accompanied the HomeView launch with updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices. It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple. Apple's work with LG and Schneider Electric to sell a suite of products alongside the HomeView was meant to make it easier to add smart home products to a household. Kaiann Drance, Apple's vice president of product marketing for home products, said the devices can be added with a single tap, similar to Apple's first-party devices such as AirPods. "For people who haven't experienced the Home ecosystem or haven't gone further than maybe a product here or there, I think this is a great opportunity to look," Drance told Reuters in an interview. Ben Wood, chief analyst and chief marketing officer for CCS Insight, said that at first glance Apple's partnership with the two outside firms looked like a break with its usual practice of fully controlling its hardware. During a video demonstrating the device, Apple showed the HomeView, which is meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops, and its Siri virtual assistant juggling voice requests from multiple members of a family at the same time. To pull in private data from messages and calendars, the HomeView relies on a user having an iPhone that's been recently unlocked and connected to the same home network. The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said. Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet's Google Home speakers and Amazon's Echo line. Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers. “Apple has the brand, technology and loyal customers to make a serious impact, but it is playing catch-up with rivals that have a far stronger presence," Pescatore said. Fragmentation among various companies' "smart" home products and the difficulty of connecting them has proved a hurdle to the market's growth although there is hope that AI-enabled devices from Apple, Google and Amazon could make integration more seamless. "Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can't run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement," said Mohit Agrawal, Research Director at Counterpoint. "Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it." Apple's $299 price for HomeView is above Amazon's Echo Show 8 at $199.99 and Google's Nest Hub at $99.99, as it seeks a bigger role in connected homes. NEW YORK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market.
It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition and will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success.
The company's services revenue has come under regulatory pressure, although that could also eventually get a boost from the new suite of devices.

Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet's Google Home speakers and Amazon's Echo line.
Apple accompanied the HomeView launch with updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices.
The launches also coincide with growing worries that connected devices, including refrigerators and smart TVs, could be vulnerable to hackers.
The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said.

To pull in private data from messages and calendars, the HomeView relies on a user having an iPhone that's been recently unlocked and connected to the same home network.

coreStoryFacts.text: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.

And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.
By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.

HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.
With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030.

HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.
HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry.
HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system.
Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple.

To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio.
A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension.
Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds.
Apple® today introduced Apple HomeView™, designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it.

HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses. 2 Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13. “Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.” HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable. The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer. A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation. A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests. Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer. With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before. 3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro. With Siri AI built into HomeView, even users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery. With powerful new features and unrivaled privacy protections, Siri remains the world’s most private digital assistant. The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background. By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill. The Flow face dynamically responds to physical presence and movement, transforming HomeView into a piece of interactive art. And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments. HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio. HomeView makes it effortless for users to stay in touch and get things done around the house. FaceTime and Center Stage keep everyone framed perfectly, even when participants are moving around the room. 6 Messages can be read and answered by voice or with the onscreen keyboard. Intercom lets users broadcast a quick message to a single room or the whole house — reaching other HomeView and HomePod speakers, as well as personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. In the kitchen, HomeView is the perfect sous chef, converting recipes from the web into step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking, so users can stay focused on what’s cooking. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.

And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.
By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.

HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.
With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030.

HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.
HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry.
HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system.
Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple.

To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio.
A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension.
Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds.

NEW YORK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market.
It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition and will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success.
The company's services revenue has come under regulatory pressure, although that could also eventually get a boost from the new suite of devices.

Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet's Google Home speakers and Amazon's Echo line.
Apple accompanied the HomeView launch with updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices.
The launches also coincide with growing worries that connected devices, including refrigerators and smart TVs, could be vulnerable to hackers.
The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said.

Apple unveiled the HomeView smart display and the Apple Home Collection accessories today, aiming to expand its connected‑home footprint through AI‑powered Siri and partnerships with LG and Schneider Electric. NEW YORK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market. The HomeView device, which starts at $299 and starts shipping next month, is Apple's latest entry into a highly competitive market for connected home devices. It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition and will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own. "Apple needs to demonstrate that its AI capabilities can deliver meaningful benefits beyond basic voice commands, simplifying everyday tasks and bringing greater intelligence to the home," said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore. Investors are looking more closely at Apple's hardware sales for growth. The company's services revenue has come under regulatory pressure, although that could also eventually get a boost from the new suite of devices. "The objective seems to be to drive high-margin 'Services' revenue via Apple TV, Apple Pay and iCloud," said Melissa Otto, head of Visible Alpha Research at S&P Global Market Intelligence, noting that Apple's 2027 services revenue is forecast to rise 12% to $138 billion. "Growth in Apple's lucrative subscription services may be the gateway to earnings growth increases over the next two years." Apple this summer upgraded Siri's capabilities with assistance from Google but analysts said it is unclear whether its AI assistant is competitive enough to lure consumers to a crowded connected home device space. The device features a 7-inch screen — which Apple said is to make it fit into a home without being too imposing — similar to Apple's "sunflower" iMac from the 2000s. And while it features a menu of square app icons like an iPhone or iPad that change depending on which user is recognized, Apple showed it being used more often via voice with its Siri AI assistant. The launches also coincide with growing worries that connected devices, including refrigerators and smart TVs, could be vulnerable to hackers. Apple accompanied the HomeView launch with updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices. It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple. Apple's work with LG and Schneider Electric to sell a suite of products alongside the HomeView was meant to make it easier to add smart home products to a household. Kaiann Drance, Apple's vice president of product marketing for home products, said the devices can be added with a single tap, similar to Apple's first-party devices such as AirPods. "For people who haven't experienced the Home ecosystem or haven't gone further than maybe a product here or there, I think this is a great opportunity to look," Drance told Reuters in an interview. Ben Wood, chief analyst and chief marketing officer for CCS Insight, said that at first glance Apple's partnership with the two outside firms looked like a break with its usual practice of fully controlling its hardware. During a video demonstrating the device, Apple showed the HomeView, which is meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops, and its Siri virtual assistant juggling voice requests from multiple members of a family at the same time. To pull in private data from messages and calendars, the HomeView relies on a user having an iPhone that's been recently unlocked and connected to the same home network. The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said. Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet's Google Home speakers and Amazon's Echo line. Fragmentation among various companies' "smart" home products and the difficulty of connecting them has proved a hurdle to the market's growth although there is hope that AI-enabled devices from Apple, Google and Amazon could make integration more seamless. "Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can't run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement," said Mohit Agrawal, Research Director at Counterpoint. "Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it." Apple's $299 price for HomeView is above Amazon's Echo Show 8 at $199.99 and Google's Nest Hub at $99.99, as it seeks a bigger role in connected homes. story.title: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home - Apple

facts.text: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.

And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.
By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.

HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.
With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030.

HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.
HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry.
HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system.
Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple.

To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio.
A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension.
Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds.

Apple said the device will begin shipping October 30, with a U.S. price of $149.

Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line.
It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition, will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success.
Other bells and whistles Apple’s HomeView launch was accompanied by updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices.
Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers.

Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own.
It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple.

extraction.body: NEW YORK -- Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market. The HomeView device, which starts at US$299 and starts shipping next month, is Apple’s latest entry into a highly competitive market for home connected devices. It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition, will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own. “Apple needs to demonstrate that its AI capabilities can deliver meaningful benefits beyond basic voice commands, simplifying everyday tasks and bringing greater intelligence to the home,” said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore. “The opportunity is considerable, given its vast installed base, but reliability, trust and ease of use will ultimately determine whether consumers embrace these features,” he added. “AI alone will not be enough to convince households to invest in more devices.” Investors are looking more closely at Apple’s hardware sales for growth as the company’s services revenue has come under regulatory pressure. Apple this summer upgraded Siri’s capabilities with assistance from Google but analysts said it is unclear whether its AI assistant is competitive enough to lure consumers to a crowded connected home device space. The launches also coincide with growing worries that connected devices, including refrigerators and smart TVs, could be vulnerable to hackers. Other bells and whistles Apple’s HomeView launch was accompanied by updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices. It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple. “It is interesting to see Apple partnering with LG and Schneider, as it typically likes to have full control of the hardware it sells,” said Ben Wood, co-founder of CCS Insight. ”However, looking closely, it appears like there has been very deep collaboration between Apple and these partners to ensure the design, engineering and experience closely match what users would expect from Apple.” During a video demonstrating the device, Apple showed the HomeView, which is meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops, and its Siri virtual assistant juggling voice requests from multiple members of a family at the same time. The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said. Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line. Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers. “Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can’t run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement,” said Mohit Agrawal, Research Director at Counterpoint. “Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it.” Apple $299 price for HomeView is above Amazon’s Echo Show 8 at $199.99 and Google’s Nest Hub at $99.99, as it seeks a bigger role in connected homes. The new Apple TV 4K enters the market at $299, more than double the price of its predecessor and in line with Nvidia’s Shield TV Pro, while rival offerings from Amazon, Google and Roku cost $200 or less. Shares were up 1.6 per cent in early Tuesday trading. Apple stock has gained 25 per cent so far this year, outperforming the large-cap Nasdaq 100, which is up 21 per cent for the same period. (Reporting by Stephen Nellis in San Francisco; Additional reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru; Editing by David Gaffen and Christian Plumb)

extraction.body: NEW YORK -- Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market. The HomeView device, which starts at US$299 and starts shipping next month, is Apple’s latest entry into a highly competitive market for home connected devices. It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition, will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own. “Apple needs to demonstrate that its AI capabilities can deliver meaningful benefits beyond basic voice commands, simplifying everyday tasks and bringing greater intelligence to the home,” said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore. “The opportunity is considerable, given its vast installed base, but reliability, trust and ease of use will ultimately determine whether consumers embrace these features,” he added. “AI alone will not be enough to convince households to invest in more devices.” Investors are looking more closely at Apple’s hardware sales for growth as the company’s services revenue has come under regulatory pressure. Apple this summer upgraded Siri’s capabilities with assistance from Google but analysts said it is unclear whether its AI assistant is competitive enough to lure consumers to a crowded connected home device space. The launches also coincide with growing worries that connected devices, including refrigerators and smart TVs, could be vulnerable to hackers. Other bells and whistles Apple’s HomeView launch was accompanied by updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices. It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple. “It is interesting to see Apple partnering with LG and Schneider, as it typically likes to have full control of the hardware it sells,” said Ben Wood, co-founder of CCS Insight. ”However, looking closely, it appears like there has been very deep collaboration between Apple and these partners to ensure the design, engineering and experience closely match what users would expect from Apple.” During a video demonstrating the device, Apple showed the HomeView, which is meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops, and its Siri virtual assistant juggling voice requests from multiple members of a family at the same time. The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said. Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line. Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers. “Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can’t run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement,” said Mohit Agrawal, Research Director at Counterpoint. “Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it.” Apple $299 price for HomeView is above Amazon’s Echo Show 8 at $199.99 and Google’s Nest Hub at $99.99, as it seeks a bigger role in connected homes. The new Apple TV 4K enters the market at $299, more than double the price of its predecessor and in line with Nvidia’s Shield TV Pro, while rival offerings from Amazon, Google and Roku cost $200 or less. Shares were up 1.6 per cent in early Tuesday trading. Apple stock has gained 25 per cent so far this year, outperforming the large-cap Nasdaq 100, which is up 21 per cent for the same period. (Reporting by Stephen Nellis in San Francisco; Additional reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru; Editing by David Gaffen and Christian Plumb)

NEW YORK -- Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market.

Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line.
It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition, will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success.
Other bells and whistles Apple’s HomeView launch was accompanied by updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices.
Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers.

Apple stock has gained 25 per cent so far this year, outperforming the large-cap Nasdaq 100, which is up 21 per cent for the same period. (Reporting by Stephen Nellis in San Francisco; Additional reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru; Editing by David Gaffen and Christian Plumb)

Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own.
It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple.

NEW YORK, Oct 13 (Reuters) – Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market.

Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line.
Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers.
The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said.

“Apple needs to demonstrate that its AI capabilities can deliver meaningful benefits beyond basic voice commands, simplifying everyday tasks and bringing greater intelligence to the home,” said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore.
Apple accompanied the HomeView launch with updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices.
It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple.

“However, looking closely, it appears like there has been very deep collaboration between Apple and these partners to ensure the design, engineering and experience closely match what users would expect from Apple,” he said.
Shares were up about 1% in Tuesday afternoon trading after earlier touching a record.
Apple stock has gained 25% so far this year, outperforming the large-cap Nasdaq 100, which is up 21% for the same period.
“Apple has the brand, technology and loyal customers to make a serious impact, but it is playing catch-up with rivals that have a far stronger presence,” Pescatore said.

Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own.
“For people who haven’t experienced the Home ecosystem or haven’t gone further than maybe a product here or there, I think this is a great opportunity to look,” Drance told Reuters in an interview.

extraction.body: NEW YORK, Oct 13 (Reuters) – Apple on Tuesday launched a raft of smart products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, in a bet that its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant can help it carve out a bigger share of the highly competitive connected home market. The HomeView device, which starts at $299 and starts shipping next month, is Apple’s latest entry into a highly competitive market for connected home devices. It will feature a 7-inch screen and face recognition and will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own. “Apple needs to demonstrate that its AI capabilities can deliver meaningful benefits beyond basic voice commands, simplifying everyday tasks and bringing greater intelligence to the home,” said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore. Investors are looking more closely at Apple’s hardware sales for growth. The company’s services revenue has come under regulatory pressure, although that could also eventually get a boost from the new suite of devices. “The objective seems to be to drive high-margin ‘Services’ revenue via Apple TV, Apple Pay and iCloud,” said Melissa Otto, head of Visible Alpha Research at S&P Global Market Intelligence, noting that Apple’s 2027 services revenue is forecast to rise 12% to $138 billion. “Growth in Apple’s lucrative subscription services may be the gateway to earnings growth increases over the next two years.” Apple this summer upgraded Siri’s capabilities with assistance from Google but analysts said it is unclear whether its AI assistant is competitive enough to lure consumers to a crowded connected home device space. The device features a 7-inch screen — which Apple said is to make it fit into a home without being too imposing — similar to Apple’s “sunflower” iMac from the 2000s. And while it features a menu of square app icons like an iPhone or iPad that change depending on which user is recognized, Apple showed it being used more often via voice with its Siri AI assistant. The launches also coincide with growing worries that connected devices, including refrigerators and smart TVs, could be vulnerable to hackers. Apple accompanied the HomeView launch with updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices. It also introduced a range of accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple. Apple’s work with LG and Schneider Electric to sell a suite of products alongside the HomeView was meant to make it easier to add smart home products to a household. Kaiann Drance, Apple’s vice president of product marketing for home products, said the devices can be added with a single tap, similar to Apple’s first-party devices such as AirPods. “For people who haven’t experienced the Home ecosystem or haven’t gone further than maybe a product here or there, I think this is a great opportunity to look,” Drance told Reuters in an interview. Ben Wood, chief analyst and chief marketing officer for CCS Insight, said that at first glance Apple’s partnership with the two outside firms looked like a break with its usual practice of fully controlling its hardware. “However, looking closely, it appears like there has been very deep collaboration between Apple and these partners to ensure the design, engineering and experience closely match what users would expect from Apple,” he said. During a video demonstrating the device, Apple showed the HomeView, which is meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops, and its Siri virtual assistant juggling voice requests from multiple members of a family at the same time. To pull in private data from messages and calendars, the HomeView relies on a user having an iPhone that’s been recently unlocked and connected to the same home network. The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said. Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line. Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers. “Apple has the brand, technology and loyal customers to make a serious impact, but it is playing catch-up with rivals that have a far stronger presence,” Pescatore said. Fragmentation among various companies’ “smart” home products and the difficulty of connecting them has proved a hurdle to the market’s growth although there is hope that AI-enabled devices from Apple, Google and Amazon could make integration more seamless. “Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can’t run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement,” said Mohit Agrawal, Research Director at Counterpoint. “Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it.” Apple’s $299 price for HomeView is above Amazon’s Echo Show 8 at $199.99 and Google’s Nest Hub at $99.99, as it seeks a bigger role in connected homes. The new Apple TV 4K enters the market at $299, more than double the price of its starting price of its predecessor and in line with Nvidia’s Shield TV Pro, while rival offerings from Amazon, Google and Roku cost $200 or less. Shares were up about 1% in Tuesday afternoon trading after earlier touching a record. Apple stock has gained 25% so far this year, outperforming the large-cap Nasdaq 100, which is up 21% for the same period. Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own.

Investors are looking more closely at Apple’s hardware sales for growth. The company’s services revenue has come under regulatory pressure, although that could also eventually get a boost from the new suite of devices.
